translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 248

sentences.zh: 【唐紀六十四】起閼逢困敦閏月，盡屠維大荒落，凡五年有奇。

translations.literal: [Tang Annals 64] Beginning in the intercalary month of the year jiazi, ending in the year xinyou, in all a little more than five years.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Annals 64: from the intercalary month of the jiazi year through the xinyou year, covering a little more than five years in all.

sentences.zh: 武宗至道昭肅孝皇帝下會昌四年（

translations.literal: Under Emperor Wuzong Zhaosu the Filial, Huichang year 4 (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wuzong, the Filial and Sagely, Huichang year 4 (

sentences.zh: 甲子，公元八四四年）

translations.literal: jiazi, CE 844)
translations.idiomatic: jiazi, 844 CE)

sentences.zh: 閏月，壬戌，以中書侍郎、同平章事李紳同平章事，充淮南節度使。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on the day renxu, Li Shen, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Director of the Chancellery, was appointed Associate Director of the Chancellery and made military governor of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on the day renxu, Li Shen—Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Director of the Chancellery—was confirmed as Associate Director of the Chancellery and assigned as military governor of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 李德裕奏：「鎮州奏事官高迪密陳意見二事：其一，以為『賊中好為偷兵術，潛抽諸處兵聚於一處，官軍多就迫逐，以致失利；

translations.literal: Li Deyu memorialized: "The Zhenzhou memorial officer Gao Di secretly submitted two opinions: First, he held that 'among the rebels they are fond of the tactic of stealing troops—secretly drawing soldiers from various places to mass them in one spot; government troops often press in pursuit and thereby suffer defeat;
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu memorialized: "Gao Di, the Zhenzhou liaison officer, privately offered two suggestions. First: the rebels favor a 'stolen troops' stratagem—they quietly strip men from scattered garrisons and concentrate them in one place. Our armies habitually chase after them and come to grief.

sentences.zh: 經一兩月，又偷兵詣他處。

translations.literal: after one or two months they again steal troops and go to another place.
translations.idiomatic: After a month or two they shift the same trick to another sector.

sentences.zh: 官軍須知此情，自非來攻城柵，慎勿與戰。

translations.literal: Government troops must know this situation; unless the enemy comes to attack a walled camp, they should be careful not to give battle.
translations.idiomatic: Our commanders must understand this pattern: unless the rebels are actually assaulting a fort, they should avoid engaging them.

sentences.zh: 彼淹留不過三日，須散歸舊屯，如此數四空歸，自然喪氣。

translations.literal: They cannot linger more than three days and must disperse back to their old posts; if this happens three or four times with empty returns, naturally their morale will collapse.
translations.idiomatic: They cannot stay more than three days before scattering back to their old camps. After three or four fruitless marches their spirit will break of itself.

sentences.zh: 官軍密遣諜者詗其抽兵之處，乘虛襲之，無不捷矣。』

translations.literal: Government troops should secretly send spies to scout where they draw troops from, strike when they are weak, and there will be no failure.'
translations.idiomatic: Send spies to learn where they have stripped troops, then strike the weakened post—every such blow will succeed.'

sentences.zh: 其二，『鎮、魏屯兵雖多，終不能分賊勢。

translations.literal: Second, 'although the Zhen and Wei garrisons are many, in the end they cannot divide the rebels' strength.
translations.idiomatic: Second: 'though the Zhen and Wei armies are large, they never really split the rebel force.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why is that?

sentences.zh: 下營不離故處，每三兩月一深入，燒掠而去。

translations.literal: They encamp without leaving their old positions; every two or three months they make one deep incursion, burn and plunder, and leave.
translations.idiomatic: Their camps never move from the same spots; every two or three months they make one deep raid, burn and loot, and withdraw.

sentences.zh: 賊但固守城柵，城外百姓，賊亦不惜。

translations.literal: The rebels only hold fast to walled camps; the common people outside the walls the rebels also do not spare.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels simply sit behind their walls; they do not even spare the countryside populace.

sentences.zh: 宜令進營據其要害，以漸逼之。

translations.literal: It is fitting to order them to advance camps and seize their vital points, gradually pressing them.
translations.idiomatic: Order them to advance camps onto the rebels' vital ground and press inward step by step.

sentences.zh: 若止如今日，賊中殊不以為懼。』

translations.literal: If it stops as today, within the rebel ranks they will not be afraid at all.'
translations.idiomatic: If things stay as they are today, the rebels will feel scarcely any fear.'

sentences.zh: 望詔諸將各使知之！」

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will issue an edict so that each general may make this known!"
translations.idiomatic: I beg that an edict be sent so every commander is informed of this."

sentences.zh: 劉稹腹心將高文端降，言賊中乏食，令婦人挼穗舂之以給軍。

translations.literal: Liu Zhen's trusted general Gao Wenduan surrendered, saying that within the rebel ranks food was scarce and they had women rub ears of grain and pound them to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Wenduan, a trusted Liu Zhen commander, defected and reported that the rebels were short of food and had women thresh grain by hand to feed the troops.

sentences.zh: 德裕訪文端破賊之策，文端以為：「官軍今真攻澤州，恐多殺士卒，城未易得。

translations.literal: Deyu asked Wenduan for a strategy to defeat the rebels; Wenduan held that: "If government troops now truly attack Ze Prefecture, I fear many soldiers will be killed and the city will not be easily taken.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu asked Wenduan how to break the rebels. Wenduan said: "If our army assaults Ze Prefecture head-on, we will lose many men and still may not take the city.

sentences.zh: 澤州兵約萬五千人，賊常分兵太半，潛伏山谷，伺官軍攻城疲弊，則四集救之，官軍必失利。

translations.literal: Ze Prefecture has about fifteen thousand troops; the rebels often divide more than half their forces, lie hidden in valleys, wait until government troops are worn out from attacking the city, then gather from four sides to rescue it, and government troops will certainly suffer defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Ze holds about fifteen thousand men. The rebels habitually keep more than half their force hidden in the hills, waiting until our siege troops are exhausted, then converge from every direction—the assault will fail.

sentences.zh: 今請令陳許軍過乾河立寨，自寨城連延築為夾城，環繞澤州，日遣大軍布陳於外以扞救兵。

translations.literal: Now I ask that the Chenxu army be ordered to cross the Gan River and establish a camp, and from the camp city continuously build a twin-walled encirclement ringing Ze Prefecture, daily sending large forces to deploy formations outside to ward off relief troops.
translations.idiomatic: Instead, have the Chenxu army cross the Gan River and build a camp, then extend linked walls in a double enclosure all around Ze. Each day station a large force outside to block relief columns.

sentences.zh: 賊見圍城將合，必出大戰；

translations.literal: When the rebels see the siege walls about to close, they will certainly come out for a great battle;
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the ring about to close, the rebels will surely sally out for a decisive fight;

sentences.zh: 待其敗北，然後乘勢可取。」

translations.literal: wait until they are defeated and flee north, then ride the momentum and they can be taken."
translations.idiomatic: once they are beaten and retreating, we can take the city at a stroke."

sentences.zh: 德裕奏請詔示王宰。

translations.literal: Deyu memorialized asking that an edict be issued to inform Wang Zai.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu memorialized that this plan be sent to Wang Zai by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 文端又言：「固鎮寨四崖懸絕，勢不可攻。

translations.literal: Wenduan also said: "The Guzhen camp's four cliffs hang sheer; by its terrain it cannot be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Wenduan added: "The Guzhen stockade sits on sheer cliffs on all four sides and cannot be stormed.

sentences.zh: 然寨中無水，皆飲澗水，在寨東南約一里許。

translations.literal: Yet within the camp there is no water; all drink stream water about one li southeast of the camp.
translations.idiomatic: But the camp has no water of its own; everyone drinks from a stream about a li to the southeast.

sentences.zh: 宜令王逢進兵逼之，絕其水道，不過三日，賊必棄寨遁去，官軍即可追躡。

translations.literal: It is fitting to order Wang Feng to advance troops and press them, cut off their water route—in no more than three days the rebels will surely abandon the camp and flee, and government troops can immediately pursue.
translations.idiomatic: Have Wang Feng advance and seize the stream. Within three days the rebels will abandon the camp; our troops can then run them down.

sentences.zh: 前十五里至青龍寨，亦四崖懸絕，水在寨外，可以前法取也。

translations.literal: Fifteen li ahead is Qinglong Camp, likewise with four sheer cliffs; water is outside the camp, and the previous method can be used to take it.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen li farther on lies Qinglong Camp, equally cliff-bound with its water outside—the same method will work there.

sentences.zh: 其東十五里則沁州城。」

translations.literal: Fifteen li east of that is Qin Prefecture city."
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen li east of that stands Qin Prefecture city."

sentences.zh: 德裕奏請詔示王逢。

translations.literal: Deyu memorialized asking that an edict be issued to inform Wang Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu memorialized that these instructions be sent to Wang Feng by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 文端又言：「都頭王釗將萬兵戍洺州，劉稹既族薛茂卿，又誅刑洺救援兵馬使談朝義兄弟三人，釗自是疑懼。

translations.literal: Wenduan also said: "Commander Wang Zhao leads ten thousand troops garrisoning Ming Prefecture. After Liu Zhen had the Xue Maqing clan executed and also put to death the Ming relief army commander Tan Chaoyi and his three brothers, Zhao from that time was suspicious and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Wenduan also said: "Commander Wang Zhao holds Ming Prefecture with ten thousand men. Liu Zhen had already wiped out the Xue Maqing clan and executed Tan Chaoyi, the Ming relief commander, together with his three brothers. Zhao has been fearful and suspicious ever since.

sentences.zh: 稹遣使召之，釗不肯入，士卒皆嘩噪，釗必不為稹用。

translations.literal: Zhen sent envoys to summon him; Zhao refused to enter, the soldiers all clamored, and Zhao will certainly not serve Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen sent to summon him, but Zhao would not come in; his troops are in an uproar. He will not fight for Zhen.

sentences.zh: 但釗及士卒家屬皆在潞州，又士卒恐己降為官軍所殺，招之必不肯來。

translations.literal: But Zhao and the soldiers' families are all in Lu Prefecture, and moreover the soldiers fear that if they surrender they will be killed by government troops; if summoned they will certainly not come.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhao's and his men's families are all in Lu Prefecture, and the troops fear that surrender means execution. They will not come if we merely call.

sentences.zh: 惟有諭意於釗，使引兵入潞州取稹。

translations.literal: Only by conveying our intent to Zhao, making him lead troops into Lu Prefecture to seize Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: We should instead make our terms clear to Zhao: lead your men into Lu Prefecture and seize Liu Zhen.

sentences.zh: 事成之日，許除別道節度使，仍厚有賜與，庶幾肯從。」

translations.literal: On the day the affair succeeds, promise to appoint him military governor of another circuit and still give generous rewards—then perhaps he will consent."
translations.idiomatic: Promise him a military governorship on another circuit and rich rewards when he succeeds—then he may agree."

sentences.zh: 德裕奏請詔何弘潛遣人諭以此意。

translations.literal: Deyu memorialized asking that an edict order He Hongjing to send someone to explain this intent.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu memorialized that He Hongjing be ordered by edict to send an envoy with this proposal.

sentences.zh: 劉稹年少懦弱，押牙王協、宅內兵馬使李士貴用事，專聚貨財，府庫充溢，而將士有功無賞，由是人心離怨。

translations.literal: Liu Zhen was young and weak; the yamen guard Wang Xie and the household army commander Li Shigui held power, devoted solely to amassing wealth until the treasuries overflowed, while officers and soldiers who had merit received no reward—thereby hearts turned away in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhen was young and timid. Wang Xie, his yamen guard, and Li Shigui, commander of the household troops, ran affairs, hoarding wealth until the vaults brimmed while meritorious officers went unrewarded. Disaffection spread through the ranks.

sentences.zh: 劉從諫妻裴氏，冕之支孫也，憂稹將敗，其弟問典兵在山東，欲召之使掌軍政。

translations.literal: Liu Congjian's wife Lady Pei was a collateral descendant of Pei Mian; fearing Zhen would be defeated, she wished to summon her younger brother Wen, who commanded troops in Shandong, to make him manage military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Pei, Liu Congjian's widow and a collateral descendant of Pei Mian, feared Zhen's fall. Her younger brother Wen commanded troops in Shandong; she wanted to recall him to take charge of the army.

sentences.zh: 士貴恐問至奪己權，且洩其奸狀，乃曰：「山東之事仰成於五舅，若召之，是無三州也。」

translations.literal: Shigui feared that if Wen arrived he would seize his authority and also expose his wicked conduct, so he said: "Shandong affairs rely on completion by the Fifth Uncle; if he is summoned, that means losing the three prefectures."
translations.idiomatic: Shigui feared Wen would displace him and expose his corruption. He said: "Shandong has been entrusted to the Fifth Uncle; recall him and we lose the three prefectures."

sentences.zh: 乃上。

translations.literal: He then went up.
translations.idiomatic: He then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 王協薦王釗為洺州都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: Wang Xie recommended Wang Zhao as Ming Prefecture commander of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xie recommended Wang Zhao as overall commander of Ming Prefecture's forces.

sentences.zh: 釗得眾心，而多不遵使府約束，同列高元武、安玉言其有貳心。

translations.literal: Zhao won the troops' hearts, yet often did not follow the headquarters' regulations; his colleagues Gao Yuanwu and An Yu said he had a divided heart.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao won the soldiers' loyalty but often ignored headquarters orders. His peers Gao Yuanwu and An Yu accused him of disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 稹召之，釗辭以「到洺州未立少功，實所慚恨，乞留數月，然後詣府。」

translations.literal: Zhen summoned him; Zhao declined on the grounds that "since arriving at Ming Prefecture I have achieved little merit—this is truly my shame and regret; I beg to remain several months and then come to headquarters."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen summoned him. Zhao pleaded: "I have done little since reaching Ming and am ashamed to face headquarters. Grant me a few more months, then I will come in."

sentences.zh: 許之，王協請稅商人，每州遣軍將一人主之，名為稅商，實籍編戶家貲，至於什器無所遺，皆估為絹匹，十分取其二，率高其估。

translations.literal: Permission was granted. Wang Xie requested to tax merchants: each prefecture would send one army officer to supervise it, called "merchant tax," but in fact they registered registered households' property; even utensils were not omitted—all were appraised as silk bolts, two-tenths taken, and the appraisals were usually set high.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen agreed. Wang Xie proposed a merchant tax: each prefecture would send an officer to levy it. In practice they inventoried every registered household's assets down to household goods, appraised everything in silk bolts, and took two-tenths—always at inflated valuations.

sentences.zh: 民竭浮財及糗糧輸之，不能充，皆璟璟不安。

translations.literal: The people exhausted floating wealth and dry provisions to pay it yet could not fill the quota; all were anxious and uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: People drained their movable property and grain stores and still could not meet the demand; everywhere there was unrest and fear.

sentences.zh: 軍將劉溪尤貪殘，劉從諫棄不用。

translations.literal: The army officer Liu Xi was especially greedy and cruel; Liu Congjian had cast him aside and not used him.
translations.idiomatic: The officer Liu Xi was notoriously rapacious; Liu Congjian had long refused to employ him.

sentences.zh: 溪厚賂王協，協以刑州富商最多，命溪主之。

translations.literal: Xi gave Wang Xie heavy bribes; Xie, because Xing Prefecture had the most wealthy merchants, ordered Xi to supervise it.
translations.idiomatic: Xi bribed Wang Xie heavily. Xie assigned him Xing Prefecture, where the richest merchants were concentrated.

sentences.zh: 裴問所將兵號「夜飛」，多富商子弟，溪至，悉拘其父兄。

translations.literal: The troops Pei Wen commanded were called "Night Flight," mostly sons of wealthy merchants; when Xi arrived he detained all their fathers and elder brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Wen's unit, the "Night Flight," was largely drawn from merchant families. When Xi arrived he seized their fathers and elder brothers.

sentences.zh: 軍士訴於問，問為之請，溪不許，以不遜語答之。

translations.literal: The soldiers appealed to Wen; Wen pleaded for them, but Xi would not agree and answered with insolent words.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers appealed to Wen, who interceded for them. Xi refused and answered with insults.

sentences.zh: 問怒，密與麾下謀殺溪歸國，並告刺史崔嘏，嘏從之。

translations.literal: Wen was enraged, secretly plotted with his subordinates to kill Xi and return to allegiance with the state, and also informed Prefect Cui Gu, who agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Wen, furious, secretly plotted with his men to kill Xi and submit to the court. He told Prefect Cui Gu, who agreed.

sentences.zh: 丙子，嘏、問閉城，斬城中大將四人，請降於王元逵。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi, Gu and Wen closed the city, beheaded four great generals in the city, and requested surrender to Wang Yuankui.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingzi, Gu and Wen shut the gates, executed four senior officers in the city, and offered surrender to Wang Yuankui.

sentences.zh: 時高元武在黨山，聞之，亦降。

translations.literal: At that time Gao Yuanwu was at Dang Mountain; on hearing this, he also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yuanwu, then at Dang Mountain, heard the news and surrendered as well.

sentences.zh: 先是使府賜洺州軍士布，人一端，尋有帖以折冬賜。

translations.literal: Earlier the headquarters had granted Ming Prefecture soldiers cloth, one bolt per man; soon there was a notice for a mid-winter grant.
translations.idiomatic: Headquarters had earlier given each Ming soldier a bolt of cloth, and a notice soon followed promising a mid-winter bonus.

sentences.zh: 會稅商軍將至洺州，王釗因人不安，謂軍士曰：「留後年少，政非己出。

translations.literal: Just as the merchant-tax army officer was about to reach Ming Prefecture, Wang Zhao, because the people were uneasy, said to the soldiers: "The acting commissioner is young; government is not his own.
translations.idiomatic: As the tax officer was about to reach Ming, Zhao, sensing the troops' unrest, told them: "The young commissioner does not truly rule.

sentences.zh: 今倉庫充實，足支十年，豈可不少散之以慰勞苦之士！

translations.literal: Now the storehouses are full, enough to last ten years—how can we not distribute a little to comfort the toiling soldiers!
translations.idiomatic: The warehouses are full enough for ten years. Should we not open them a little to reward men who have suffered?

sentences.zh: 使貼不可用也。」

translations.literal: The headquarters notice cannot be used."
translations.idiomatic: Ignore headquarters' notice."

sentences.zh: 乃擅開倉庫，給士卒人絹一匹，谷十二石，士卒大喜。

translations.literal: He then on his own authority opened the storehouses and gave each soldier one bolt of silk and twelve piculs of grain; the soldiers were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the stores on his own authority and gave each man a bolt of silk and twelve piculs of grain. The troops were overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 釗遂閉城請降於何弘敬。

translations.literal: Zhao then closed the city and requested surrender to He Hongjing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao then shut the gates and offered surrender to He Hongjing.

sentences.zh: 安玉在磁州，聞二州降，亦降於弘敬。

translations.literal: An Yu was at Ci Prefecture; on hearing that the two prefectures had surrendered, he also surrendered to Hongjing.
translations.idiomatic: An Yu at Ci Prefecture, hearing that both prefectures had submitted, surrendered to Hongjing as well.

sentences.zh: 堯山都知失馬使魏元談等降於王元逵，元逵以其久不下，皆殺之。

translations.literal: The Yaoshan commander Wei Yuantan and others surrendered to Wang Yuankui; Yuankui, because they had long not submitted, killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yuantan, commander at Yaoshan, and others surrendered to Wang Yuankui, who executed them all for having held out so long.

sentences.zh: 八月，辛卯，鎮、魏奏邢、洺、磁三州降，宰相入賀。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day xinmao, Zhen and Wei reported that Xing, Ming, and Ci—the three prefectures—had surrendered; the chief ministers entered to congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the day xinmao, the Zhen and Wei armies reported the surrender of Xing, Ming, and Ci. The chief ministers came in to offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 李德裕曰：「昭義根本盡在山東，三州降，則上黨不日有變矣。」

translations.literal: Li Deyu said: "Zhaoyi's foundation is entirely in Shandong; with the three prefectures surrendered, Shangdang will before long have change."
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu said: "Zhaoyi's strength lay entirely in Shandong. With those three prefectures gone, Shangdang will collapse before long."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「郭誼必梟劉稹以自贖。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Guo Yi will certainly present Liu Zhen's head to redeem himself."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Guo Yi is sure to deliver Liu Zhen's head to save his own skin."

sentences.zh: 德裕曰：「誠如聖料。」

translations.literal: Deyu said: "It is truly as Your Sagely foresight judged."
translations.idiomatic: Deyu said: "Your Majesty reads the situation exactly right."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「於今所宜先處者何事？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Of what should be handled first at present?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked: "What should we settle first, now?"

sentences.zh: 德裕請以給事中盧弘止為三州留後，曰：「萬一鎮、魏請占三州，朝廷難於可否。」

translations.literal: Deyu requested that Supervising Secretary Lu Hongzhi be made regent of the three prefectures, saying: "In the event Zhen and Wei request to occupy the three prefectures, the court will find it hard to grant or refuse."
translations.idiomatic: Deyu proposed appointing Supervising Secretary Lu Hongzhi regent of the three prefectures. "If Zhen and Wei ask to keep them," he said, "the court will be hard pressed to refuse yet should not concede."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 詔山南東道兼昭義節度使盧鈞乘驛赴鎮。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Lu Jun, military governor of Shannan East Circuit who also held Zhaoyi, to ride post-horses and proceed to his post.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Lu Jun—governor of Shannan East who also held Zhaoyi—to hurry to his command by post relay.

sentences.zh: 潞人聞三州降，大懼。

translations.literal: The people of Lu heard the three prefectures had surrendered and were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Prefecture heard that the three prefectures had fallen, panic spread.

sentences.zh: 郭誼、王協謀殺劉稹以自贖，稹再從兄中軍使匡周兼押牙，誼患之，言於稹曰：「十三郎在牙院，諸將皆莫敢言事，恐為十三郎所疑而獲罪，以此失山東。

translations.literal: Guo Yi and Wang Xie plotted to kill Liu Zhen to redeem themselves; Zhen's second cousin once removed, the central army commander Kuang Zhou who also held the yamen guard, was a worry to Yi, who said to Zhen: "The Thirteenth Son is in the yamen courtyard; the generals all dare not speak on affairs, fearing the Thirteenth Son's suspicion and punishment—thereby we lost Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yi and Wang Xie plotted to kill Liu Zhen and save themselves. Zhen's cousin Kuang Zhou commanded the central army and also held the yamen guard; Yi feared him. He told Zhen: "With the Thirteenth Son in the headquarters courtyard, no general dares speak freely—we lost Shandong because of it.

sentences.zh: 今誠得十三郎不入，則諸將始敢盡言，采於眾人，必獲長策。」

translations.literal: Now if we can truly keep the Thirteenth Son from entering, then the generals will begin to dare speak fully; gathering from the multitude, we will certainly obtain a long-term plan."
translations.idiomatic: Keep him out, and the officers will finally speak plainly. Take counsel from all sides and we are sure to find a way forward."

sentences.zh: 稹召匡周諭之，使稱疾不入。

translations.literal: Zhen summoned Kuang Zhou and instructed him to plead illness and not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen summoned Kuang Zhou and told him to stay away on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 匡周怒曰：「我在院中，故諸將不敢有異圖；

translations.literal: Kuang Zhou angrily said: "While I am in the courtyard, therefore the generals dare not have divergent designs;
translations.idiomatic: Kuang Zhou flared up: "While I am here, the generals dare not plot;

sentences.zh: 我出院，家必滅矣！」

translations.literal: if I leave the courtyard, the family will certainly be destroyed!"
translations.idiomatic: if I leave, our house is finished!"

sentences.zh: 稹固請之，匡周不得已，彈指而出。

translations.literal: Zhen firmly pressed him; Kuang Zhou had no choice, snapped his fingers, and went out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen insisted. Kuang Zhou had no choice: he snapped his fingers and walked out.

sentences.zh: 誼令稹所親董可武說稹曰：「山東之叛，事由五舅，城中人人誰敢相保！

translations.literal: Yi ordered Zhen's intimate Dong Kewu to persuade Zhen, saying: "The Shandong rebellion was caused by the Fifth Uncle; within the city, who dares guarantee anyone's safety!
translations.idiomatic: Yi had Zhen's confidant Dong Kewu tell him: "The Fifth Uncle caused the Shandong revolt. In this city, who can feel safe?

sentences.zh: 留後今欲何如？」

translations.literal: What does the acting commissioner wish to do now?"
translations.idiomatic: What does the commissioner intend to do now?"

sentences.zh: 稹曰：「今城中尚有五萬人，且當閉門堅守耳。」

translations.literal: Zhen said: "Now within the city there are still fifty thousand men; for the time being we should shut the gates and hold firm."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen said: "We still have fifty thousand men in the city. We should shut the gates and hold on."

sentences.zh: 可武曰：』非良策也。

translations.literal: Kewu said: "That is not a good plan.
translations.idiomatic: Kewu said: "That is no good plan.

sentences.zh: 留後不若束身歸朝，如張元益，不失作刺史。

translations.literal: The acting commissioner would do better to bind himself and return to the court, like Zhang Yuanyi, and not fail to become a prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Better surrender yourself to the court, as Zhang Yuanyi did—you would still receive a prefecture.

sentences.zh: 且以郭誼為留後，俟得節之日，徐奉太夫人及室家金帛歸之東都，不亦善乎！」

translations.literal: Moreover appoint Guo Yi acting commissioner; when the day of receiving the commission arrives, slowly escort the Dowager Lady and the household's gold and silk back to the Eastern Capital—is that not also good!"
translations.idiomatic: Make Guo Yi acting commissioner for now. Once he receives the commission, your mother and family can take their wealth back to Luoyang in good time. Would that not be best?"

sentences.zh: 稹曰：「誼安肯如是？」

translations.literal: Zhen said: "How would Yi be willing to act thus?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhen said: "Would Yi truly do that?"

sentences.zh: 可武曰：「可武已與之重誓，必不負也。」

translations.literal: Kewu said: "Kewu has already sworn a heavy oath with him; he will certainly not betray you."
translations.idiomatic: Kewu said: "I have sworn a solemn oath with him. He will not betray you."

sentences.zh: 及引誼入。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led Yi in.
translations.idiomatic: Then he brought Yi in.

sentences.zh: 稹與之密約既定，乃白其母。

translations.literal: After Zhen and he had set their secret agreement, he then informed his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhen and Yi had sealed their secret pact, Zhen told his mother.

sentences.zh: 母曰：「歸朝誠為佳事，但恨已晚。

translations.literal: His mother said: "Returning to the court is truly a fine matter, but I regret it is already late.
translations.idiomatic: His mother said: "Surrender would indeed be wise, but I fear it is too late.

sentences.zh: 吾有弟不能保，安能保郭誼！

translations.literal: I could not even protect my own younger brother—how can I protect Guo Yi!
translations.idiomatic: I could not even save my own brother—how can I trust Guo Yi!

sentences.zh: 汝自圖之！」

translations.literal: You must plot for yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: You must decide for yourself!"

sentences.zh: 稹乃素服出門，以母命署誼都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: Zhen then in plain dress went out the gate and, by his mother's order, appointed Yi commander of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen put on plain clothes, went out, and by his mother's authority appointed Yi commander of the army.

sentences.zh: 王協已戒諸將列於外廳，誼拜謝稹已，出見諸將，稹治裝於內廳。

translations.literal: Wang Xie had already warned the generals to line up in the outer hall; after Yi bowed in thanks to Zhen, he went out to see the generals while Zhen packed in the inner hall.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xie had already assembled the generals in the outer hall. Yi bowed to Zhen, went out to face the officers, while Zhen packed in the inner hall.

sentences.zh: 李士貴聞之，帥後院兵數千攻誼。

translations.literal: Li Shigui heard this and led several thousand rear-courtyard troops to attack Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shigui heard of it and led several thousand household guards against Yi.

sentences.zh: 誼叱之曰：「何不自取賞物，乃欲與李士貴同死乎！」

translations.literal: Yi shouted at them: "Why not take reward goods for yourselves—do you wish to die together with Li Shigui!"
translations.idiomatic: Yi shouted: "Why not seize your share of the loot instead of dying with Li Shigui!"

sentences.zh: 軍士乃退，共殺士貴。

translations.literal: The soldiers then withdrew and together killed Shigui.
translations.idiomatic: The troops fell back and together killed Shigui.

sentences.zh: 誼易置將吏，部署軍士，一夕俱定。

translations.literal: Yi replaced generals and officials, deployed the soldiers, and in one night all was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Yi replaced officers, redeployed the troops, and within a single night had everything under control.

sentences.zh: 明日，使董可武入謁稹曰：「請議公事。」

translations.literal: The next day he sent Dong Kewu in to visit Zhen, saying: "I request to discuss official business."
translations.idiomatic: The next day he sent Dong Kewu to see Zhen: "We must discuss state business."

sentences.zh: 稹曰：「何不言之！」

translations.literal: Zhen said: "Why not speak of it!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhen said: "Speak here, then!"

sentences.zh: 可武曰：「恐驚太夫人。」

translations.literal: Kewu said: "I fear alarming the Dowager Lady."
translations.idiomatic: Kewu said: "I fear distressing your mother."

sentences.zh: 乃引稹步出牙門，至北宅，置酒作樂。

translations.literal: He then led Zhen on foot out the yamen gate to the North Residence, set out wine, and made music.
translations.idiomatic: He led Zhen on foot out through the headquarters gate to the North Residence, where wine and music were prepared.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，乃言：「今日之事欲全太尉一家，須留後自圖去就，則朝廷必垂矜閔。」

translations.literal: When the wine was deep, he then said: "Today's affair wishes to preserve the Grand Marshal's whole household; the acting commissioner must himself plot his going or staying—then the court will certainly extend pity."
translations.idiomatic: When the wine had gone deep, he said: "To save your whole house, Commissioner, you must decide your own course. The court will surely show mercy."

sentences.zh: 稹曰：「如所言，稹之心也。」

translations.literal: Zhen said: "As you have said—that is Zhen's own heart."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen said: "What you say is exactly what I wish."

sentences.zh: 可武遂前執其手，，崔率度自後斬之，因收稹宗族，匡周以下至襁褓中子皆殺之。

translations.literal: Kewu then stepped forward and seized his hand; Cui Shualv from behind beheaded him, then rounded up Zhen's clan—from Kuang Zhou down to infants still in swaddling clothes, all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Kewu seized his hands from the front while Cui Shualv struck from behind and cut off his head. They then seized Zhen's entire clan and killed everyone from Kuang Zhou down to babes in arms.

sentences.zh: 又殺劉從諫父子所厚善者張谷、陳揚庭、李仲京、郭台、王羽、韓茂章、茂實、王渥、賈庠等凡十二家，並其子侄甥婿無遺。

translations.literal: They also killed those whom Liu Congjian and his son had deeply favored—Zhang Gu, Chen Yangting, Li Zhongjing, Guo Tai, Wang Yu, Han Maozhang, Maoshi, Wang Wo, Jia Xiang, and twelve households in all—together with their sons, nephews, sons-in-law, and sons of daughters, leaving none.
translations.idiomatic: They also slaughtered twelve households whom Liu Congjian and his son had favored—Zhang Gu, Chen Yangting, Li Zhongjing, Guo Tai, Wang Yu, Han Maozhang and Maoshi, Wang Wo, Jia Xiang, and others—sparing not a son, nephew, son-in-law, or grandson.

sentences.zh: 仲京，訓之兄；

translations.literal: Zhongjing was Xun's elder brother;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjing was the elder brother of Li Xun;

sentences.zh: 台，行餘之子。

translations.literal: Tai was Xingyu's son.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tai was the son of Guo Xingyu.

sentences.zh: 羽，涯之從孫；

translations.literal: Yu was Ya's collateral grandson;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu was a collateral descendant of Wang Ya;

sentences.zh: 茂章、茂實，約之子；

translations.literal: Maozhang and Maoshi were Yue's sons;
translations.idiomatic: Han Maozhang and Maoshi were sons of Han Yue;

sentences.zh: 渥，璠之子。

translations.literal: Wo was Fan's son.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wo was the son of Wang Fan.

sentences.zh: 庠，餗之子也。

translations.literal: Xiang was Su's son.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xiang was the son of Jia Su.

sentences.zh: 甘露之亂，仲京等亡歸從諫，從諫撫養之。

translations.literal: In the Sweet Dew turmoil, Zhongjing and the others fled and returned to Congjian, who nurtured them.
translations.idiomatic: After the Sweet Dew Affair, Zhongjing and the others had fled to Liu Congjian, who sheltered and raised them.

sentences.zh: 凡軍中有小嫌者，誼日有所誅，流血成泥。

translations.literal: For anyone in the army with the slightest grudge, Yi daily executed some; blood flowed like mud.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone in the army who bore the slightest grudge was put to death day after day until blood ran like mud.

sentences.zh: 乃函稹首，遣使奉表及書，降於王宰。

translations.literal: He then boxed Zhen's head, sent envoys bearing a memorial and letter, and surrendered to Wang Zai.
translations.idiomatic: He placed Zhen's head in a box, sent envoys with a memorial and letter of surrender, and submitted to Wang Zai.

sentences.zh: 首過澤州，劉公直舉營慟哭，亦降於宰。

translations.literal: When the head passed Ze Prefecture, Liu Gongzhi raised the whole camp in wailing lament and also surrendered to Zai.
translations.idiomatic: As the head passed through Ze Prefecture, Liu Gongzhi led his entire camp in mourning and surrendered to Zai as well.

sentences.zh: 乙未，宰以狀聞。

translations.literal: On the day yiwei, Zai reported the situation.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yiwei, Zai reported the victory to the court.

sentences.zh: 丙申，宰相入賀。

translations.literal: On the day bingshen, the chief ministers entered to congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingshen, the chief ministers came in to offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 李德裕奏：「今不須復置邢、洺、磁留後，但遣盧弘止宣慰三州及成德、魏博兩道。」

translations.literal: Li Deyu memorialized: "Now there is no need again to appoint regents for Xing, Ming, and Ci; only send Lu Hongzhi to proclaim comfort to the three prefectures and the two circuits of Chengde and Weibo."
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu memorialized: "We need no longer appoint regents for Xing, Ming, and Ci. Send Lu Hongzhi to proclaim comfort to those three prefectures and to the Chengde and Weibo circuits."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「郭誼宜如何處之？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "How should Guo Yi be dealt with?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked: "What should be done with Guo Yi?"

sentences.zh: 德裕對曰：「劉稹騃孺子耳，阻兵拒命，皆誼為之謀主。

translations.literal: Deyu replied: "Liu Zhen was but a foolish child; blocking troops and defying orders—all were plotted by Yi as chief strategist.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu answered: "Liu Zhen was a witless boy. Yi was the mastermind who armed the rebellion and defied the throne.

sentences.zh: 及勢孤力屈，又賣稹以求賞。

translations.literal: When his position was isolated and strength exhausted, he again sold Zhen to seek reward.
translations.idiomatic: When his power collapsed, he sold out Zhen for a reward.

sentences.zh: 此而不誅，何以懲惡！

translations.literal: If this man is not executed, how can evil be punished!
translations.idiomatic: If we spare him, how will we punish treachery!

sentences.zh: 宜及諸軍在境，並誼等誅之！」

translations.literal: It is fitting, while the various armies are still in the territory, to execute Yi and the rest together!"
translations.idiomatic: Execute Yi and his accomplices while our armies are still on the ground!"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕意亦以為然。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "My mind also holds it so."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "I agree."

sentences.zh: 乃詔石雄將七千人入潞州，以應謠言。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered Shi Xiong to lead seven thousand men into Lu Prefecture, in accord with a popular saying.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Shi Xiong to lead seven thousand men into Lu Prefecture—fulfilling a popular prophecy.

sentences.zh: 杜悰以饋運不給，謂誼等可赦，上熟視不應。

translations.literal: Du Cong, because supply transport was insufficient, said Yi and the others could be pardoned; the Emperor stared at him intently and did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Du Cong, citing supply shortages, argued that Yi and the others should be pardoned. The Emperor fixed him with a long stare and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 德裕曰：「今春澤潞未平，太原復擾，自非聖斷堅定，二寇何由可平！

translations.literal: Deyu said: "This spring Ze and Lu were not yet pacified, and Taiyuan was disturbed again—if not for Your Sagely resolve being firm, how could the two rebels have been subdued!
translations.idiomatic: Deyu said: "This spring Ze and Lu were still in revolt and Taiyuan was in turmoil again. Without Your Majesty's firm resolve, how could both rebellions have been crushed!

sentences.zh: 外議以為若在先朝，赦之久矣。」

translations.literal: Outside opinion holds that under the previous reign they would long ago have been pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: Outsiders say that under the previous reign they would have been pardoned long ago."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿不知文宗心地不與卿合，安能議乎！」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "You do not know that Emperor Wenzong's mind was not in accord with yours—how could he have deliberated thus!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "You forget that Emperor Wenzong's mind was not yours. How could he have acted as you would!"

sentences.zh: 罷盧鈞山南東道，專為昭義節度使。

translations.literal: Lu Jun was removed from Shannan East Circuit and made solely military governor of Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jun was relieved of Shannan East and appointed solely military governor of Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，劉稹傳首至京師。

translations.literal: On the day wuxu, Liu Zhen's transmitted head reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuxu, Liu Zhen's head arrived at the capital.

sentences.zh: 詔：「昭義五州給復一年，軍行所過州縣免今年秋稅。

translations.literal: An edict: "The five prefectures of Zhaoyi shall receive tax relief for one year; prefectures and counties through which the army passed are exempted from this year's autumn tax.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "The five Zhaoyi prefectures shall receive a year's tax relief, and every county and prefecture the army passed through is exempt from this autumn's levy.

sentences.zh: 昭義自劉從諫以來，橫增賦斂，悉從蠲免。

translations.literal: Since Liu Congjian's time Zhaoyi had arbitrarily increased levies—all are remitted from exemption.
translations.idiomatic: All arbitrary levies imposed since Liu Congjian's day were abolished.

sentences.zh: 所藉土團並縱遣歸農。

translations.literal: Local militia that had been conscripted were all released and sent back to farming.
translations.idiomatic: Conscripted local militia were disbanded and sent home to farm.

sentences.zh: 諸道將士有功者，等級加賞。」

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers of the various circuits who had merit received graded additional rewards."
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious officers and soldiers from every circuit were rewarded according to rank."

sentences.zh: 郭誼既殺劉稹，日望旌節，既久不聞問，乃曰：「必移它鎮。」

translations.literal: After Guo Yi had killed Liu Zhen, he daily looked for the commission of office; having long heard nothing, he then said: "I must surely be transferred to another post."
translations.idiomatic: After killing Liu Zhen, Guo Yi waited daily for his commission as military governor. When no word came for a long time, he said: "They must be transferring me to another circuit."

sentences.zh: 於是閱鞍馬，治行裝。

translations.literal: He then inspected saddles and horses and prepared traveling gear.
translations.idiomatic: He inspected his horses and packed for the journey.

sentences.zh: 及聞石雄將至，懼失色。

translations.literal: When he heard Shi Xiong was about to arrive, he turned pale with fear.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Shi Xiong was coming, he turned pale with fear.

sentences.zh: 雄至，誼等參賀畢，敕使張仲清曰：「郭都知告身來日當至，諸高班告身在此，晚牙來受之！」

translations.literal: When Xiong arrived, after Yi and the others had paid their respects, the edict envoy Zhang Zhongqing said: "Commander Guo's commission of appointment will arrive tomorrow; the senior officers' commissions are here—come receive them at the evening roll call!"
translations.idiomatic: When Xiong arrived, Yi and the others paid their respects. The imperial envoy Zhang Zhongqing announced: "Commander Guo's commission will arrive tomorrow. The senior officers' commissions are here—come to the evening assembly to receive them!"

sentences.zh: 乃以河中兵環球場，晚牙，誼等至，唱名引入，凡諸將桀黠拒官軍者，悉執送京師。

translations.literal: He then had Hezhong troops surround the ball ground; at evening roll call, when Yi and the others arrived, names were called and they were led in—all fierce and cunning generals who had resisted government troops were seized and sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhong troops ringed the parade ground. At the evening assembly, as Yi and the others arrived, their names were called and they were led in. Every fierce commander who had resisted the imperial army was seized and sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 加何弘敬同平章事。

translations.literal: He Hongjing was promoted to Associate Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He Hongjing was made Associate Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 丁未，詔發劉從諫屍，暴於潞州市三日，石雄取其屍置球場斬坐刀之。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei, an edict ordered Liu Congjian's corpse exhumed and exposed in Lu Prefecture city for three days; Shi Xiong took the corpse, placed it on the ball ground, and executed it by seated waist-slicing.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingwei, an edict ordered Liu Congjian's corpse exhumed and displayed in Lu Prefecture for three days. Shi Xiong then had the body brought to the parade ground and executed by waist-slicing in the seated position.

sentences.zh: 戊申，加李德裕太尉、趙國公，德裕固辭。

translations.literal: On the day wushen, Li Deyu was promoted to Grand Marshal and Duke of Zhao; Deyu firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wushen, Li Deyu was made Grand Marshal and Duke of Zhao. He firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「恨無官賞卿耳！

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I regret only that there is no higher office with which to reward you!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "I only regret that there is no higher rank with which to reward you!

sentences.zh: 卿若不應得，朕必不與卿。」

translations.literal: If you were not deserving, I would certainly not give it to you."
translations.idiomatic: If you did not deserve it, I would never grant it."

sentences.zh: 初，李德裕以「韓全義以來，將帥出征屢敗，其弊有三：一者，詔令下軍前者，日有三四，宰相多不預聞。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Deyu held that "since Han Quanyi, generals on campaign have repeatedly been defeated; the abuses are three: First, edicts reaching the army ahead number three or four daily, and the chief ministers often do not hear of them beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Deyu had said: "Since Han Quanyi's time, campaigning generals have suffered repeated defeats. There are three abuses. First: three or four edicts a day reach the army before the chief ministers even hear of them.

sentences.zh: 二者，監軍各以意見指揮軍事，將帥不得專進退。

translations.literal: Second, army supervisors each command military affairs according to their own opinions, and generals cannot exclusively advance or retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Second: each army supervisor commands according to his own whim, and the generals cannot advance or retreat on their own authority.

sentences.zh: 三者每軍各有宦者為監使，悉選軍中驍勇數百為牙隊，其在陳戰鬥者，皆怯弱之士。

translations.literal: Third, each army has eunuchs as supervisory commissioners; all select several hundred of the army's fiercest and bravest for the guard corps, while those who fight in formation are all timid and weak soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Third: every army has eunuch supervisors who pick several hundred of the fiercest men for their personal guard, leaving only the timid and weak to fight in the line.

sentences.zh: 每戰，監使自有信旗，乘高立馬，以牙隊自衛，視軍勢小卻，輒引旗先走，陳從而潰。」

translations.literal: In every battle the supervisor has his own signal banner, mounts a horse on high ground, uses the guard corps to protect himself, and when he sees the army's momentum slightly recede, immediately pulls his banner and flees first—the formation follows and collapses."
translations.idiomatic: In every battle the supervisor rides to high ground with his own signal banner, surrounded by his guard. At the slightest setback he pulls his banner and flees first, and the whole line routs behind him."

sentences.zh: 德裕乃與樞密使楊欽義、劉行深議，約敕監軍不得預軍政，每兵千人聽監使取十人自衛，有功隨例沾賞。

translations.literal: Deyu then deliberated with Privy Council commissioners Yang Qinyi and Liu Xingshen, agreeing that edicts should forbid army supervisors from interfering in military government; per thousand troops the supervisor might take ten men for self-defense, and merit would bring reward by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu then worked out reforms with Privy Council commissioners Yang Qinyi and Liu Xingshen: supervisors were forbidden to interfere in command; each might take only ten men per thousand for a bodyguard; and they would share in rewards when merit was earned.

sentences.zh: 二樞密皆以為然，白上行之。

translations.literal: Both Privy Council commissioners held it right and reported to the Emperor to implement it.
translations.idiomatic: Both commissioners approved and reported the plan to the Emperor, who put it into effect.

sentences.zh: 自御回鶻至澤潞罷兵，皆守此制。

translations.literal: From resisting the Uyghurs through the Ze-Lu campaign until arms were laid down, all observed this system.
translations.idiomatic: From the campaign against the Uyghurs through the Ze-Lu war until arms were laid down, this system was maintained throughout.

sentences.zh: 自非中書進詔意，更無它詔自中出者。

translations.literal: Unless the Secretariat advanced the edict's intent, no other edict issued from within.
translations.idiomatic: No edict reached the armies except through the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 號令既簡，將帥得以施其謀略，故所向有功。

translations.literal: Orders being thus simplified, generals could deploy their stratagems, and therefore wherever they went they had achievement.
translations.idiomatic: With orders simplified, generals could execute their own plans, and wherever they marched they prevailed.

sentences.zh: 自用兵以來，河北三鎮每遣使者至京師，李德裕常面諭之曰：「河朔兵力雖強，不能自立，須借朝廷官爵威命以安軍情。

translations.literal: Since troops had been employed, whenever the three Hebei posts sent envoys to the capital, Li Deyu often instructed them face to face, saying: "Though Heshuo's military strength is great, it cannot stand alone; it must borrow the court's offices, titles, and authoritative mandate to settle the troops' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever envoys from the three Hebei posts came to the capital during the war, Li Deyu would tell them plainly: "However strong Heshuo's armies may be, you cannot stand alone. You need the court's offices and authority to keep your soldiers loyal.

sentences.zh: 歸語汝使：與其使大將邀宣慰敕使以求官爵，何如自奮忠義，立功立事，結知明主，使恩出朝廷，不亦榮乎！

translations.literal: Return and tell your commissioner: rather than having great generals waylay comfort-and-reassurance edict envoys to seek offices and titles, how much better to rouse your own loyalty and righteousness, establish merit and achievement, win the knowing favor of a wise sovereign, and let grace come from the court—is that not also glorious!
translations.idiomatic: Go back and tell your master: instead of having your generals ambush imperial envoys to extort titles, why not win merit through loyal service, earn the favor of a wise emperor, and receive honors that truly come from the court? Would that not be more glorious!

sentences.zh: 且以耳目所及者言之，李載義在幽州，為國家盡忠平滄景，及為軍中所逐，不失作節度使，後鎮太原，位至宰相。

translations.literal: Moreover, speaking of what eye and ear have reached: Li Zaiyi was at Youzhou, loyally served the state in pacifying Cang and Jing; though driven out by the army, he still did not fail to become military governor, later governed Taiyuan, and rose to chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Consider what you have seen with your own eyes. Li Zaiyi at Youzhou loyally pacified Cang and Jing for the state. Though his troops drove him out, he still became military governor, later governed Taiyuan, and rose to chief minister.

sentences.zh: 楊志誠遣大將遮敕使馬求官，及為軍中所逐，朝廷竟不赦其罪。

translations.literal: Yang Zhicheng sent a great general to block an edict envoy's horse to seek office; when he was driven out by the army, the court in the end did not pardon his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhicheng sent a general to stop an imperial envoy and demand office. When his own troops drove him out, the court never pardoned his crime.

sentences.zh: 此二人禍福足以觀矣。」

translations.literal: These two men's fortune and misfortune are sufficient to observe."
translations.idiomatic: The fates of these two men speak for themselves."

sentences.zh: 德裕復以其言白上，上曰：「要當如此明告之。」

translations.literal: Deyu again reported these words to the Emperor; the Emperor said: "They must indeed be told this plainly."
translations.idiomatic: Deyu repeated this to the Emperor, who said: "They must be told this plainly."

sentences.zh: 由是三鎮不敢有異志。

translations.literal: Thereby the three posts did not dare harbor divergent intentions.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the three posts dared not harbor rebellious thoughts.

sentences.zh: 九月，詔以澤州隸河陽節度。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, an edict placed Ze Prefecture under Heyang military governorship.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, an edict placed Ze Prefecture under the Heyang military governorship.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，盧鈞入潞州。

translations.literal: On the day dingsi, Lu Jun entered Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingsi, Lu Jun entered Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 鈞素寬厚愛人，劉稹未平，鈞已領昭義節度，襄州士卒在行營者，與潞人戰，常對陳揚鈞之美。

translations.literal: Jun was by nature generous and loving toward people; before Liu Zhen was pacified, Jun already held the Zhaoyi military governorship, and Xiang Prefecture soldiers in the field camp, when fighting Lu men, often praised Jun's virtues across the battle lines.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was known for his generosity and kindness. Even before Liu Zhen fell, he had been appointed military governor of Zhaoyi, and Xiang soldiers in the field camp often praised his virtues to the Lu troops across the battle lines.

sentences.zh: 及赴鎮，入天井關，昭義散卒歸之道，鈞皆厚撫之，人情大洽，昭議遂安。

translations.literal: When he went to his post and entered Tianjing Pass, Zhaoyi scattered soldiers returning on the road were all generously comforted by Jun; popular sentiment was greatly harmonious, and Zhaoyi was thereby settled.
translations.idiomatic: When he went to take up his post and entered Tianjing Pass, he generously treated every scattered Zhaoyi soldier he met on the road. Hearts warmed to him, and Zhaoyi was soon at peace.

sentences.zh: 劉稹將郭誼、王協、劉公直、安全慶、李道德、劉佐堯、劉開德、董可武等至京師，皆斬之。

translations.literal: Liu Zhen's generals Guo Yi, Wang Xie, Liu Gongzhi, An Quanqing, Li Daode, Liu Zuoyao, Liu Kaide, Dong Kewu, and others reached the capital—all were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhen's generals Guo Yi, Wang Xie, Liu Gongzhi, An Quanqing, Li Daode, Liu Zuoyao, Liu Kaide, Dong Kewu, and others were brought to the capital and all beheaded.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：董重質之在淮西，郭誼之在昭義，吳元濟、劉稹，如木偶人在伎兒之手耳。

translations.literal: Your subject Guang says: With Dong Chongzhi in Huaixi and Guo Yi in Zhaoyi, Wu Yuanji and Liu Zhen were like wooden puppets in the hands of showmen.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang comments: With Dong Chongzhi in Huaixi and Guo Yi in Zhaoyi, Wu Yuanji and Liu Zhen were no more than wooden puppets in the hands of puppeteers.

sentences.zh: 彼二人者，始則勸人為亂，終則賣主規利，其死固有餘罪。

translations.literal: Those two men at first urged others to rebel, and in the end sold their masters to seek profit; their deaths indeed left guilt to spare.
translations.idiomatic: Those two men first incited rebellion and then betrayed their masters for gain. Their deaths were richly deserved.

sentences.zh: 然憲宗用之於前，武宗誅之於後，臣愚以為皆失之。

translations.literal: Yet Emperor Xianzong employed them before, and Emperor Wuzong executed them after—I, your foolish subject, hold that both were in error.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Emperor Xianzong used them before, and Emperor Wuzong executed them after. In my humble view, both rulers were wrong.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why so?

sentences.zh: 賞奸，非義也；

translations.literal: Rewarding the wicked is not righteous;
translations.idiomatic: To reward traitors is unjust;

sentences.zh: 殺降，非信也。

translations.literal: killing those who surrender is not faithful.
translations.idiomatic: to kill men who have surrendered is faithless.

sentences.zh: 失義與信，何以為國！

translations.literal: Losing righteousness and faith—how can one be a state!
translations.idiomatic: Without righteousness and faith, how can a state endure!

sentences.zh: 昔漢光武待王郎、劉盆子止於不死，知其非力竭則不降故也。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Guangwu of Han treated Wang Lang and Liu Penzi only to the point of not killing them, knowing that unless strength was exhausted they would not surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu of Han spared Wang Lang and Liu Penzi only their lives, knowing that rebels surrender only when their strength is spent.

sentences.zh: 樊崇、徐宣、王元、牛邯之徒，豈非助亂之人乎？

translations.literal: Fan Chong, Xu Xuan, Wang Yuan, Niu Han, and their kind—were they not men who aided rebellion?
translations.idiomatic: Were Fan Chong, Xu Xuan, Wang Yuan, Niu Han, and their like not agents of rebellion?

sentences.zh: 而光武弗殺。

translations.literal: Yet Guangwu did not kill them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Guangwu did not execute them.

sentences.zh: 蓋以既受其降，則不可復誅故也。

translations.literal: This was because once their surrender had been accepted, they could not again be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had accepted their surrender, he could not put them to death.

sentences.zh: 若既赦而復逃亡叛亂，則其死固無辭矣！

translations.literal: If after pardon they again fled, rebelled, and made turmoil, then their death would indeed admit no excuse!
translations.idiomatic: If, after pardon, they fled and rebelled again, execution would be fully justified!

sentences.zh: 如誼等，免死流之遠方，沒齒不還，可矣；

translations.literal: Men like Yi could have been spared death and exiled to distant regions, never to return within their lives—that would have sufficed;
translations.idiomatic: Men like Yi should have been spared and exiled to distant lands, never to return—that would have been enough;

sentences.zh: 殺之，非也！

translations.literal: to kill them was wrong!
translations.idiomatic: to kill them was wrong!

sentences.zh: 王羽、賈庠等已為誼所殺，李德裕復下詔稱「逆賊王涯、賈餗等已就昭義誅其子孫」，宣告中外，識者非之。

translations.literal: Wang Yu, Jia Xiang, and the others had already been killed by Yi; Li Deyu again issued an edict stating "the rebel criminals Wang Ya, Jia Su, and others have already had their descendants executed at Zhaoyi," proclaiming it within and without—men of judgment disapproved.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu, Jia Xiang, and the others had already been killed by Yi. Li Deyu then issued an edict proclaiming to all within and without that "the rebel criminals Wang Ya, Jia Su, and others have had their descendants executed in Zhaoyi." Thoughtful men condemned this.

sentences.zh: 劉從諫妻裴氏亦賜死。

translations.literal: Liu Congjian's wife Lady Pei was also ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Congjian's widow Lady Pei was also ordered to take her own life.

sentences.zh: 又令昭義降將李丕、高文端、王釗等疏昭義將士與劉稹同惡者，悉誅之，死者甚眾。

translations.literal: He also ordered Zhaoyi surrendering generals Li Pi, Gao Wenduan, Wang Zhao, and others to denounce Zhaoyi officers and soldiers who shared Liu Zhen's evil—all were executed, and the dead were very many.
translations.idiomatic: He also had Zhaoyi defectors Li Pi, Gao Wenduan, Wang Zhao, and others denounce every officer and soldier who had sided with Liu Zhen. All were executed, and the dead were very numerous.

sentences.zh: 盧鈞疑其枉濫，奏請寬之，不從。

translations.literal: Lu Jun suspected this was excessive and indiscriminate, memorialized asking leniency, and was not followed.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jun suspected wholesale injustice and memorialized for clemency, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 昭義屬城有嘗無禮於王元逵者，元逵推求得二十餘人，斬之。

translations.literal: In a subordinate city of Zhaoyi there were those who had once been disrespectful to Wang Yuankui; Yuankui tracked them down and got more than twenty men, whom he beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: In one Zhaoyi subordinate city, men who had once insulted Wang Yuankui were hunted down; he beheaded more than twenty of them.

sentences.zh: 餘眾懼，復閉城自守。

translations.literal: The remaining multitude were afraid and again closed the city to hold it themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The rest of the populace, terrified, shut the gates and held the city again.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，李德裕等奏：「寇孽既平，盡為國家城鎮，豈可令元逵窮兵攻討！

translations.literal: On the day wuchen, Li Deyu and others memorialized: "The rebel brood being already pacified, all are the state's towns and cities—how can Yuankui be allowed to exhaust troops in attack!
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuchen, Li Deyu and others memorialized: "The rebels are crushed and these are imperial towns. How can we let Yuankui press the attack to the bitter end!

sentences.zh: 望遣中使賜城內將士敕，招安之，仍詔元逵引兵歸鎮，並詔盧鈞自遣使安撫。」

translations.literal: We hope to send a palace envoy to grant an edict to the city's officers and soldiers and win them by reassurance, and also order Yuankui to lead troops back to his post, and order Lu Jun on his own to send envoys to pacify."
translations.idiomatic: Send a palace envoy with an edict to reassure the garrison, order Yuankui to withdraw to his post, and let Lu Jun send his own envoys to pacify them."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，李德裕等請上尊號，且言：「自古帝王，成大功必告天地。

translations.literal: On the day yihai, Li Deyu and others requested that the Emperor accept a honorific title, and moreover said: "From antiquity emperors who achieved great merit must report to Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yihai, Li Deyu and others asked the Emperor to accept a honorific title, saying: "Since antiquity, emperors who achieved great deeds have reported them to Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 父，宣懿太后祔廟，陛下未嘗親謁。」

translations.literal: Your father, Empress Dowager Xuanyi, was enshrined in the ancestral temple, yet Your Majesty has never personally paid visit."
translations.idiomatic: Your father lies enshrined with Empress Dowager Xuanyi, yet Your Majesty has never visited the temple in person."

sentences.zh: 上瞿然曰：「郊廟之禮，誠宜亟行，至於徽稱，非所敢當！」

translations.literal: The Emperor started and said: "The suburban and temple rites truly ought to be hurriedly performed; as for an honorific title, it is not what I dare accept!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor started and said: "The suburban and temple rites should indeed be performed at once. As for a honorific title, I dare not accept it!"

sentences.zh: 凡五上表，乃許之。

translations.literal: In all they submitted five memorials before he permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: After five memorials he finally consented.

sentences.zh: 李德裕奏：「據幽州奏事官言：詗知回鶻上下離心，可汗欲之安西，其部落言親戚皆在唐，不如歸唐。

translations.literal: Li Deyu memorialized: "According to the Youzhou memorial officer: scouting has learned that above and below the Uyghurs are divided in heart; the qaghan wishes to go to Anxi, while his tribes say their kin are all in Tang and it would be better to return to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu memorialized: "The Youzhou liaison officer reports that the Uyghurs are divided. The qaghan wants to go west to Anxi, but his tribes say their kin are all in Tang and they would rather submit to Tang.

sentences.zh: 又與室韋已相失，計其不日來降，或自相殘滅。

translations.literal: They have also already fallen out with the Shiwei; it is calculated that before long they will come to surrender, or destroy one another.
translations.idiomatic: They have also broken with the Shiwei. They will likely surrender soon or destroy one another.

sentences.zh: 望遣識事中使賜仲武詔，諭以鎮、魏已平昭義，惟回鶻未滅，仲武猶帶北面招討使，宜早思立功。」

translations.literal: We hope to send a Supervising Secretary as envoy to grant Zhongwu an edict, informing him that Zhen and Wei have already pacified Zhaoyi and only the Uyghurs are not yet destroyed; Zhongwu still bears the northern campaign commissioner title and ought early to think of establishing merit."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that an envoy be sent to grant Zhongwu an edict, telling him that Zhen and Wei have pacified Zhaoyi and only the Uyghurs remain. Zhongwu still holds the northern campaign commission and should seek merit while he can."

sentences.zh: 李德裕怨太子太傅、東都留守牛僧孺、湖州刺史李宗閔，言於上曰：「劉從諫據上黨十年，太和中入朝，僧孺、宗閔執政，不留之，加宰相縱去，以成今日之患，竭天下力乃能取之，皆二人之罪也。」

translations.literal: Li Deyu resented Grand Mentor and Eastern Capital regent Niu Sengru and Huzhou Prefect Li Zongmin, and said to the Emperor: "Liu Congjian held Shangdang for ten years; in the Taihe era he entered court—Sengru and Zongmin held government, did not detain him, added him as chief minister and let him go, thereby creating today's calamity; exhausting the empire's strength was needed to take it—all is the crime of those two men."
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu bore a grudge against Niu Sengru, Grand Mentor and regent of the Eastern Capital, and Li Zongmin, prefect of Huzhou. He told the Emperor: "Liu Congjian held Shangdang for ten years. During the Taihe era he came to court while Sengru and Zongmin were in power. They did not detain him but made him chief minister and let him return—creating today's disaster. Only by exhausting the empire's strength could we recover the region. The fault lies with those two men."

sentences.zh: 德裕又使人於潞州求僧孺、宗閔與從諫交通書疏，無所得，乃令孔目官鄭慶言從諫每得僧孺、宗閔書疏，皆自焚毀。

translations.literal: Deyu also sent men to Lu Prefecture to seek correspondence between Sengru, Zongmin, and Congjian; obtaining none, he then had clerical officer Zheng Qing say that whenever Congjian received letters from Sengru and Zongmin he burned them himself.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu also sent men to Lu Prefecture to search for correspondence between Sengru, Zongmin, and Congjian. Finding none, he had a clerk named Zheng Qing claim that Congjian had burned every letter he received from Sengru and Zongmin.

sentences.zh: 詔追慶下御史台近問，中丞李回、知雜鄭亞以為信然。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Qing pursued to the Censorate for close interrogation; Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Hui and Supervisory Censor Zheng Ya held it credible.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Qing brought before the Censorate for interrogation. Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Hui and Supervisory Censor Zheng Ya found his testimony credible.

sentences.zh: 河南少尹呂述與德裕書，言稹破報至，僧孺出聲歎恨。

translations.literal: Henan Vice Prefect Lü Shu wrote to Deyu, saying that when the report of Zhen's defeat arrived, Sengru gave voice to sighs of regret.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Shu, vice prefect of Henan, wrote to Deyu that when news of Liu Zhen's defeat arrived, Niu Sengru sighed aloud in regret.

sentences.zh: 德裕奏述書，上大怒，以僧孺為太子少保、分司，宗閔為漳州刺史。

translations.literal: Deyu memorialized describing Shu's letter; the emperor was greatly angered and made Sengru Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent with a nominal post, and Zongmin Prefect of Zhang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu submitted a memorial recounting Lü Shu's letter. The emperor flew into a rage and made Niu Sengru Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent with a nominal court post, and Li Zongmin prefect of Zhang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 戊子，再貶僧孺汀州刺史，宗閔漳州長史。

translations.literal: On wuzi, Sengru was demoted again to Prefect of Ting Prefecture, Zongmin to Chief Secretary of Zhang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, Sengru was demoted again to prefect of Ting Prefecture, and Zongmin to chief secretary of Zhang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 上幸鄠校獵。

translations.literal: The emperor went to E to hold a hunting review.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went to E to hold a military hunt.

sentences.zh: 十一月，復貶牛僧孺循州長史，李宗閔長流封州。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Niu Sengru was demoted again to Chief Secretary of Xun Prefecture, and Li Zongmin was permanently exiled to Feng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Niu Sengru was demoted again to chief secretary of Xun Prefecture, and Li Zongmin was permanently banished to Feng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十二月，以忠武節度使王宰為河東節度使，河中節度使石雄為河陽節度使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Wang Zai, Military Governor of Zhongwu, was made Military Governor of Hedong, and Shi Xiong, Military Governor of Hezhong, was made Military Governor of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Wang Zai, military governor of Zhongwu, was appointed military governor of Hedong, and Shi Xiong, military governor of Hezhong, was appointed military governor of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 上幸雲陽校獵。

translations.literal: The emperor went to Yunyang to hold a hunting review.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went to Yunyang to hold a military hunt.

sentences.zh: 武宗至道昭肅孝皇帝下會昌五年（

translations.literal: Under Emperor Wuzong Zhaosu the Filial, Huichang year 5 (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wuzong, the Filial and Sagely, Huichang year 5 (

sentences.zh: 乙丑，公元八四五年）

translations.literal: yichou, CE 845)
translations.idiomatic: yichou, 845 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己酉朔，群臣上尊號曰仁聖文武章天成功神德明道大孝皇帝，尊號始無「道」字，中旨令加之。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on jiyou the new moon, the assembled ministers presented a honorific title reading Emperor Ren, Sage, Civil and Martial, Manifesting Heaven, Accomplishing Success, Divine in Virtue, Illuminating the Way, Greatly Filial; the title at first lacked the character "Way," and an imperial order from the inner court directed that it be added.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first day of the first month, jiyou, the assembled ministers offered the honorific title Emperor Ren, Sage, Civil and Martial, Manifesting Heaven, Accomplishing Success, Divine in Virtue, Illuminating the Way, Greatly Filial. The title originally lacked the word "Way," but an order from the inner court directed that it be added.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，上謁太廟。

translations.literal: On gengxu, the emperor visited the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, the emperor visited the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，祀昊天上帝，赦天下。

translations.literal: On xinhai, he sacrificed to the August Heaven, and a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, he sacrificed to the August Heaven and proclaimed a general amnesty throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 築望仙台於南郊。

translations.literal: The Terrace for Gazing upon Immortals was built at the southern suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: The Terrace for Gazing upon Immortals was built in the southern suburbs.

sentences.zh: 庚申，義安太后王氏崩。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Empress Dowager Wang of Yi'an died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, Empress Dowager Wang of Yi'an died.

sentences.zh: 以秘書監盧弘宣為義武節度使。

translations.literal: Director of the Palace Library Lu Hongxuan was made Military Governor of Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Hongxuan, director of the Palace Library, was appointed military governor of Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 弘宣性寬厚而難犯，為政簡易，其下便之。

translations.literal: Hongxuan was by nature generous and forbearing yet not to be transgressed; he governed simply and easily, and those beneath him found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxuan was generous and forbearing by nature, yet not to be crossed. He governed with simple, straightforward methods, and those under him found his rule easy to live with.

sentences.zh: 河北之法，軍中偶語者斬。

translations.literal: Under the law of Hebei, anyone who spoke casually in the army was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: In Hebei, the law held that anyone who spoke casually in the ranks was to be beheaded.

sentences.zh: 弘宣至，除其法。

translations.literal: When Hongxuan arrived, he abolished that law.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongxuan arrived, he abolished that law.

sentences.zh: 詔賜粟三十萬斛，在飛狐西，計運致之費逾於粟價，弘宣遣吏守之。

translations.literal: An edict granted three hundred thousand hu of grain west of Feihu; calculating the cost of transport, it exceeded the price of the grain itself, so Hongxuan sent officials to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted three hundred thousand hu of grain stored west of Feihu. The cost of transporting it would have exceeded the grain's value, so Hongxuan sent officials to guard the store.

sentences.zh: 會春旱，弘宣命軍民隨意自往取之，粟皆入境，約秋稔償之。

translations.literal: It happened that a spring drought struck; Hongxuan ordered soldiers and civilians to go freely and take it as they wished. The grain all entered the prefecture, with repayment promised after the autumn harvest.
translations.idiomatic: When a spring drought struck, Hongxuan let soldiers and civilians go and take the grain as they needed. All of it entered the prefecture, with repayment promised after the autumn harvest.

sentences.zh: 時成德、魏博皆饑，獨易定之境無害。

translations.literal: At the time Chengde and Weibo were both suffering famine; only within the borders of Yiding was there no harm.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Chengde and Weibo were both in famine, but Yiding alone escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 淮南節度使李紳按江都令吳湘盜用程糧錢，強娶所部百姓顏悅女，估其資裝為贓，罪當死。

translations.literal: Military Governor of Huainan Li Shen investigated Jiangdu Magistrate Wu Xiang for embezzling official travel-grain funds, forcibly marrying the daughter of a commoner under his jurisdiction named Yan Yue, and estimating her dowry and belongings as stolen goods; the crime merited death.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shen, military governor of Huainan, investigated Wu Xiang, magistrate of Jiangdu, for embezzling official travel-grain funds, forcibly marrying Yan Yue's daughter, a commoner under his jurisdiction, and treating her dowry and belongings as stolen goods. The crime merited death.

sentences.zh: 湘，武陵之兄子也，李德裕素惡武陵，議者多言其冤，諫官請覆按，詔遣監察御史崔元藻、李稠覆之。

translations.literal: Xiang was the nephew of Wu Ling's elder brother; Li Deyu had long hated Wu Ling, and many in discussion said the case was unjust. Remonstrating officials requested a reinvestigation, and an edict dispatched Supervisory Censors Cui Yuanzao and Li Chou to review it.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xiang was the nephew of Wu Ling's elder brother. Li Deyu had long hated Wu Ling, and many held that the case was unjust. Remonstrating officials asked for a reinvestigation, and the court dispatched Supervisory Censors Cui Yuanzao and Li Chou to review it.

sentences.zh: 還言：「湘盜程糧錢有實。

translations.literal: On returning they reported: "Xiang's embezzlement of travel-grain funds is substantiated.
translations.idiomatic: On their return they reported: "Wu Xiang's embezzlement of travel-grain funds is substantiated.

sentences.zh: 顏悅本衢州人，嘗為青州牙推，妻亦士族，與前獄異。」

translations.literal: Yan Yue was originally a man of Qu Prefecture and had once served as a military adjutant in Qing Prefecture; his wife was also of gentry stock, differing from the previous case."
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yue was originally from Qu Prefecture and had once served as a military adjutant in Qing Prefecture. His wife was also from a gentry family, which made this case different from the earlier one."

sentences.zh: 德裕以為無與奪，二月，貶元藻端州司戶，稠汀州司戶。

translations.literal: Deyu held that there was nothing to decide; in the second month, Yuanzao was demoted to Registrar of Duan Prefecture, and Chou to Registrar of Ting Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu held that there was nothing further to decide. In the second month, Yuanzao was demoted to registrar of Duan Prefecture and Chou to registrar of Ting Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 不復更推，亦不付法司詳斷，即如紳奏，處湘死。

translations.literal: There was no further reinvestigation, nor was the case referred to the judicial offices for detailed judgment; following Shen's memorial exactly, Xiang was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: There was no further investigation, nor was the case sent to the judicial offices for detailed judgment. Following Shen's memorial exactly, Wu Xiang was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫柳仲郢、敬晦皆上疏爭之，不納。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Grandees Liu Zhongyi and Jing Hui both submitted memorials disputing it; the court did not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Grandees Liu Zhongyi and Jing Hui both submitted memorials disputing the decision, but the court would not hear them.

sentences.zh: 稠，晉江人；

translations.literal: Chou was a man of Jinjiang;
translations.idiomatic: Chou was a native of Jinjiang;

sentences.zh: 晦，昕之弟也。

translations.literal: Hui was the younger brother of Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was the younger brother of Xin.

sentences.zh: 李德裕以柳仲郢為京兆尹。

translations.literal: Li Deyu made Liu Zhongyi Prefect of the Capital District.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu appointed Liu Zhongyi prefect of the Capital District.

sentences.zh: 素與牛僧孺善，謝德裕曰：「不意太慰恩獎及此，仰報厚德，敢不如奇章公門館！」

translations.literal: He had long been on good terms with Niu Sengru. He thanked Deyu, saying: "I did not expect the Grand Marshal's gracious award to reach this extent. Looking up to repay your deep kindness, how dare I not be like a retainer in Lord Qizhang's household!"
translations.idiomatic: He had long been friendly with Niu Sengru. Thanking Deyu, he said: "I never expected the Grand Marshal's gracious favor to reach this far. To repay such deep kindness, how could I fail to serve you as faithfully as a retainer in Lord Qizhang's household!"

sentences.zh: 德裕不以為嫌。

translations.literal: Deyu did not take it as cause for offense.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu took no offense at this.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，壬寅，以陝虢觀察使李試為冊黠戛斯可汗使。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, on renyin, Li Shi, Observation Commissioner of Shan and Guo, was made envoy to invest the Qarluk khan.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on renyin of the fourth month, Li Shi, observation commissioner of Shan and Guo, was appointed envoy to invest the Qarluk khan.

sentences.zh: 五月，壬戌，葬恭僖皇后於光陵柏城之外。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on renxu, Empress Gongxi was buried outside the cypress mound of Guang Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on renxu, Empress Gongxi was buried outside the cypress mound of Guang Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 門下侍郎、同平章事二悰罷為右僕射，中書侍郎、同平章事崔鉉罷為戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Li Jue, Vice Director of the Chancellery and Associate Grand Counselor, was removed and made Right Vice Director of the Department of State; Cui Xuan, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Counselor, was removed and made Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue, vice director of the Chancellery and associate grand counselor, was removed from office and made right vice director of the Department of State. Cui Xuan, vice director of the Secretariat and associate grand counselor, was removed and made minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，以戶部侍郎李回為中書侍郎、同平章事，判戶部如故。

translations.literal: On yichou, Li Hui, Vice Minister of Revenue, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Counselor, continuing to oversee the Ministry of Revenue as before.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Li Hui, vice minister of revenue, was appointed vice director of the Secretariat and associate grand counselor, while continuing to oversee the Ministry of Revenue as before.

sentences.zh: 祠部奏括天下寺四千六百，蘭若四萬，僧尼二十六萬五百。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites reported a tally of four thousand six hundred temples throughout the realm, forty thousand hermitages, and two hundred sixty thousand five hundred monks and nuns.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites reported a tally of four thousand six hundred temples throughout the realm, forty thousand hermitages, and two hundred sixty thousand five hundred monks and nuns.

sentences.zh: 詔冊黠戛斯可汗為宗英雄武誠明可汗。

translations.literal: An edict invested the Qarluk khan as Khan Zong, Heroic, Martial, Sincere, and Illuminating.
translations.idiomatic: An edict invested the Qarluk khan with the title Khan Zong, Heroic, Martial, Sincere, and Illuminating.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丙午朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, on bingwu the new moon, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on the first day of the seventh month, bingwu, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 上惡僧尼耗蠹天下，欲去之，道士趙歸真等復勸之。

translations.literal: The emperor hated that monks and nuns consumed and drained the realm, and wished to remove them; the Daoist Zhao Guizhen and others again urged him on.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hated how monks and nuns drained the resources of the realm and wished to remove them. The Daoist Zhao Guizhen and others urged him on again.

sentences.zh: 乃先毀山野招提、蘭若，至是，敕上都、東都兩街各留二寺，每寺留僧三十人；

translations.literal: He had first destroyed mountain and wilderness monasteries and hermitages; at this point an edict ordered that in the two wards of each of the Eastern and Western Capitals two temples be retained, with thirty monks left in each temple;
translations.idiomatic: He had already destroyed monasteries and hermitages in the mountains and wilderness. Now an edict ordered that in the two wards of each capital two temples be kept, with thirty monks left in each;

sentences.zh: 天下節度、觀察使治所及同、華、商、汝州各留一寺，分為三等：上等留僧二十人，中等留十人，下等五人。

translations.literal: at the seats of government of military governors and observation commissioners throughout the realm, and in Tong, Hua, Shang, and Ru Prefectures, one temple was to be retained in each, divided into three grades: the upper grade kept twenty monks, the middle grade ten, and the lower grade five.
translations.idiomatic: at the seats of every military governor and observation commissioner, and in Tong, Hua, Shang, and Ru Prefectures, one temple was to remain in each place, divided into three grades: twenty monks for the upper grade, ten for the middle, and five for the lower.

sentences.zh: 餘僧及尼並大秦穆護、襖僧皆勒歸俗。

translations.literal: All remaining monks and nuns, together with Nestorian priests and Zoroastrian monks, were compelled to return to lay life.
translations.idiomatic: All remaining monks and nuns, together with Nestorian priests and Zoroastrian monks, were forced to return to lay life.

sentences.zh: 寺非應留者，立期今所在毀撤，仍遣御史分道督之。

translations.literal: Temples not among those to be retained were given a fixed deadline for destruction and removal wherever they stood, and censors were dispatched by separate routes to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: Temples not on the retention list were given a fixed deadline for demolition wherever they stood, and censors were dispatched along separate routes to enforce it.
