sentences.zh: 財貨田產並沒官，寺材以葺公廨驛捨，銅像、鐘磐以鑄錢。

translations.literal: Goods, wealth, and farmland were all confiscated to the state; temple timber was used to repair government offices and post stations, and bronze images, bells, and chime stones were cast into coin.
translations.idiomatic: Goods, wealth, and farmland were all confiscated by the state. Temple timber was used to repair government offices and post stations, and bronze images, bells, and chime stones were melted down for coinage.

sentences.zh: 以山南東道節度使鄭肅檢校右僕射、同平章事。

translations.literal: Zheng Su, Military Governor of Shannan East Circuit, was made Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State and Associate Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Su, military governor of Shannan East Circuit, was appointed acting right vice director of the Department of State and associate grand counselor.

sentences.zh: 詔發昭義騎兵五百、步兵千五百戍振武，節度使盧鈞出至裴村餞之，潞卒素驕，憚於遠戍，乘醉，回旗入城，閉門大噪，均奔潞城以避之。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched five hundred cavalry and fifteen hundred infantry from Zhaoyi to garrison Zhenwu. Military Governor Lu Jun went out to Pei Village to see them off. The Lu troops had long been arrogant and feared distant garrison duty; drunk, they turned their banners and entered the city, shut the gates, and raised a great clamor. Jun fled to Lucheng to avoid them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict dispatched five hundred cavalry and fifteen hundred infantry from Zhaoyi to garrison Zhenwu. Military Governor Lu Jun went out to Pei Village to see them off. The Lu troops had long been arrogant and dreaded service far from home. Drunk, they turned their banners, marched back into the city, shut the gates, and raised a great uproar. Lu Jun fled to Lucheng to escape them.

sentences.zh: 監軍王惟直自出曉諭，亂兵擊之，傷，旬日而卒。

translations.literal: Army Supervisor Wang Weizhi went out himself to explain and persuade them; the mutinous troops struck him, wounding him, and he died ten days later.
translations.idiomatic: Army supervisor Wang Weizhi went out himself to reason with them. The mutinous troops attacked him, wounding him, and he died ten days later.

sentences.zh: 李德裕奏：「請詔河東節度使王宰以步騎一千守石會關，三千自儀州路據武安，以斷邢、洺之路；

translations.literal: Li Deyu memorialized: "I request that an edict order Wang Zai, Military Governor of Hedong, to hold Shihui Pass with one thousand infantry and cavalry, and three thousand to seize Wu'an by the route through Yi Prefecture, so as to cut the roads to Xing and Ming;
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu memorialized: "I ask that an edict order Wang Zai, military governor of Hedong, to hold Shihui Pass with one thousand infantry and cavalry, and send three thousand men by the route through Yi Prefecture to seize Wu'an, thereby cutting the roads to Xing and Ming;

sentences.zh: 又令河陽節度使石雄引兵守澤州，河中節度使韋恭甫發步騎千人戍晉州。

translations.literal: further, let Shi Xiong, Military Governor of Heyang, lead troops to hold Ze Prefecture, and Wei Gongfu, Military Governor of Hezhong, dispatch one thousand infantry and cavalry to garrison Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: further, let Shi Xiong, military governor of Heyang, lead troops to hold Ze Prefecture, and Wei Gongfu, military governor of Hezhong, dispatch one thousand infantry and cavalry to garrison Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 如此，賊必無能為。」

translations.literal: In this way the rebels will certainly be unable to act."
translations.idiomatic: In this way the rebels will be unable to act at all."

sentences.zh: 皆從之。

translations.literal: All was approved.
translations.idiomatic: All was approved.

sentences.zh: 八月，李德裕等奏：「東都九廟神主二十六，今貯於太微宮小屋，請以廢寺材復修太廟。」

translations.literal: Eighth month, Li Deyu and others memorialized: "The twenty-six spirit tablets of the nine temples of the Eastern Capital are now stored in a small building in the Palace of Great Subtlety. I request that timber from abolished temples be used to restore the Imperial Ancestral Temple."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Li Deyu and others memorialized: "The twenty-six spirit tablets of the Eastern Capital's nine ancestral temples are now stored in a small building in the Palace of Great Subtlety. We ask that timber from abolished temples be used to restore the Imperial Ancestral Temple."

sentences.zh: 壬午，詔陳釋教之弊，宣告中外。

translations.literal: On renwu, an edict set forth the evils of the Buddhist teaching and proclaimed them within and without the court.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, an edict set forth the evils of Buddhism and proclaimed them throughout the court and the realm.

sentences.zh: 凡天下所毀寺四千六百餘區，歸俗僧尼二十六萬五百人，大秦穆護、祅僧二千餘人，毀招提、蘭若四萬餘區。

translations.literal: In all, more than four thousand six hundred temple compounds were destroyed throughout the realm; two hundred sixty thousand five hundred monks and nuns returned to lay life; more than two thousand Nestorian priests and Zoroastrian monks; and more than forty thousand monasteries and hermitages were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: In all, more than four thousand six hundred temple compounds were destroyed throughout the realm. Two hundred sixty thousand five hundred monks and nuns returned to lay life, along with more than two thousand Nestorian priests and Zoroastrian monks. More than forty thousand monasteries and hermitages were demolished.

sentences.zh: 收良田數千萬頃，奴婢十五萬人。

translations.literal: Tens of millions of qing of fertile fields were confiscated, and one hundred fifty thousand male and female servants.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of millions of qing of fertile land were confiscated, along with one hundred fifty thousand male and female servants.

sentences.zh: 所留僧皆隸主客，不隸祠部。

translations.literal: The monks who were retained all came under the Ministry of Receptions and were no longer under the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The monks who remained were placed under the Ministry of Receptions rather than the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 百官奉表稱賀。

translations.literal: The hundred officials submitted memorials offering congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: The officials submitted memorials of congratulation.

sentences.zh: 尋又詔東都止留僧二十人，諸道留二十人者減其半，留十人者減三人，留五人者更不留。

translations.literal: Soon afterward another edict ordered that in the Eastern Capital only twenty monks be retained; where twenty had been kept in the various circuits, the number was halved; where ten had been kept, three were removed; and where five had been kept, none were kept at all.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward another edict ordered that the Eastern Capital keep only twenty monks. Where a circuit had been allowed twenty, the number was cut in half; where ten had been allowed, three were removed; and where five had been allowed, none were to remain.

sentences.zh: 五台僧多亡奔幽州。

translations.literal: Many monks of Wutai fled to You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Many monks from Wutai fled to You Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 李德裕召進奏官謂曰：「汝趣白本使，五台僧為將必不如幽州將，為卒必不如幽州卒，何為虛取容納之名，染於人口！

translations.literal: Li Deyu summoned the memorial-delivery officer and said: "You hurry and tell your military governor: as generals the Wutai monks will certainly be inferior to You Prefecture generals; as soldiers they will certainly be inferior to You Prefecture soldiers. Why take in vain the name of giving refuge and let the talk stain people's mouths!
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu summoned the memorial-delivery officer and said: "Go quickly and tell your military governor: Wutai monks would make worse generals than Youzhou generals and worse soldiers than Youzhou soldiers. Why take in refugees for an empty reputation and let the talk stain your name!

sentences.zh: 獨不見近日劉從諫招聚無算閒人，竟有保益！」

translations.literal: Have you alone not seen how Liu Congjian recently gathered countless idlers—and was there any benefit at all!"
translations.idiomatic: Have you not seen how Liu Congjian recently gathered countless idlers—and what benefit did it bring?"

sentences.zh: 張仲武乃封二刀付居庸關曰：「有游僧入境則斬之！」

translations.literal: Zhang Zhongwu then sealed up two swords and delivered them to Juyong Pass, saying: "If any wandering monk enters the border, behead him!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhongwu then sealed up two swords and sent them to Juyong Pass with the order: "If any wandering monk crosses the border, behead him!"

sentences.zh: 主客郎中韋博以為事不宜太過，李德裕惡之，出為靈武節度副使。

translations.literal: Wei Bo, Director in the Ministry of Receptions, held that the affair ought not go too far; Deyu resented this and sent him out as deputy military governor of Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Bo, a director in the Ministry of Receptions, held that the policy had gone too far. Deyu resented this and sent him out as deputy military governor of Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 昭義亂兵奉都將李文矩為帥，文矩不從，亂兵亦不敢害。

translations.literal: The mutinous troops of Zhaoyi raised Chief Commander Li Wenju as their leader; Wenju would not accept, and the mutinous troops also did not dare harm him.
translations.idiomatic: The mutinous Zhaoyi troops tried to make Chief Commander Li Wenju their leader. Wenju refused, and the mutineers did not dare harm him.

sentences.zh: 文矩稍以禍福諭之，亂兵漸聽命，乃遣人謝盧鈞於潞城。

translations.literal: Wenju gradually admonished them with talk of fortune and disaster; the mutinous troops gradually obeyed, and then sent a man to apologize to Lu Jun at Lucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wenju gradually reasoned with them about the consequences of fortune and disaster. The mutineers slowly came around, and then sent a man to apologize to Lu Jun at Lucheng.

sentences.zh: 均還入上黨，復遣之戍振武。

translations.literal: Jun returned to Shangdang and again dispatched them to garrison Zhenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jun returned to Shangdang and again dispatched the troops to garrison Zhenwu.

sentences.zh: 行一驛，乃潛選兵追之。

translations.literal: After they had traveled one post station, he secretly selected troops and pursued them.
translations.idiomatic: After the troops had marched one post station, he secretly selected men and pursued them.

sentences.zh: 明日，及於太平驛，盡殺之。

translations.literal: The next day he overtook them at Taiping Post and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he caught up with them at Taiping Post and killed them all.

sentences.zh: 具以狀聞，且請罷河東、河陽兵在境上者，從之。

translations.literal: He reported the full circumstances and also requested that the Hedong and Heyang troops stationed on the border be withdrawn; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He reported the full circumstances and also asked that the Hedong and Heyang troops stationed on the border be withdrawn. The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 九月，詔修東都太廟。

translations.literal: Ninth month, an edict ordered the restoration of the Imperial Ancestral Temple of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, an edict ordered the restoration of the Imperial Ancestral Temple in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 李德裕請置備邊庫，令戶部歲入錢帛十二萬緡匹，度支鹽鐵歲入錢帛十三萬緡匹，明年減其三之一，凡諸道所進助軍財貨者皆入焉，以度支郎中判之。

translations.literal: Li Deyu requested the establishment of a Border Defense Reserve Treasury, ordering the Ministry of Revenue to contribute one hundred twenty thousand strings and bolts of cash and silk annually, and the Salt and Iron Commission under the Department of Public Works to contribute one hundred thirty thousand strings and bolts annually, with one-third of each reduced the following year; all goods and wealth presented as military aid by the various circuits were to enter it, to be overseen by a Director in the Department of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu requested the establishment of a Border Defense Reserve Treasury. The Ministry of Revenue was to contribute one hundred twenty thousand strings and bolts of cash and silk each year, and the Salt and Iron Commission one hundred thirty thousand, with both amounts reduced by one-third the following year. All military aid presented by the circuits was to go into the treasury, overseen by a director in the Department of Public Works.

sentences.zh: 王才人寵冠後庭，上欲立以為後。

translations.literal: Lady Wang the Talented enjoyed favor above all others in the inner quarters, and the emperor wished to make her empress.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang the Talented was the most favored woman in the inner palace, and the emperor wished to make her empress.

sentences.zh: 李德裕以才人寒族，且無子，恐不厭天下之望，乃止。

translations.literal: Li Deyu, on the grounds that the Talented Lady was of humble clan and moreover had no son, feared she would not satisfy the hopes of the realm, and so the plan was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu argued that she came from a humble family and had no son, and feared she would not satisfy the expectations of the realm. The plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 上餌方士金丹，性加躁急，喜怒不常。

translations.literal: The emperor took the alchemists' golden elixir, and his temperament grew ever more irritable and impetuous; joy and anger were not constant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took the alchemists' golden elixir, and his temperament grew ever more irritable. His moods swung unpredictably.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，上問李德裕以外事，對曰：「陛下威斷不測，外人頗驚懼。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, the emperor questioned Li Deyu about external affairs. He replied: "Your Majesty's awesomeness and decisions are unpredictable; outsiders are quite alarmed and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, the emperor asked Li Deyu about affairs beyond the palace. He replied: "Your Majesty's awesomeness and decisions are unpredictable, and outsiders are deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 向者寇逆暴橫，固宜以威制之；

translations.literal: Formerly, when rebels and traitors were violent and overbearing, it was indeed fitting to control them with awesomeness;
translations.idiomatic: When rebels and traitors were violent and overbearing, it was right to control them with stern authority;

sentences.zh: 今天下既平，願陛下寬理之，但使得罪者無怨，為善者不驚，則為寬矣。」

translations.literal: now that the realm is already at peace, I wish Your Majesty would govern it with leniency—only let those who have offended harbor no resentment, and let those who do good feel no alarm, and that will be leniency."
translations.idiomatic: but now that the realm is at peace, I hope Your Majesty will govern with leniency. Let those who have offended feel no resentment, and let those who do good feel no alarm—that would be true leniency."

sentences.zh: 以衡山道士劉玄靜為銀青光祿大夫、崇玄館學士，賜號廣成先生，為之治崇玄館，置吏鑄印。

translations.literal: The Hengshan Daoist Liu Xuanjing was made Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Academician of the Hall of Venerating Mystery, granted the style Master Guangcheng, and for him the Hall of Venerating Mystery was furnished, with officials appointed and a seal cast.
translations.idiomatic: The Hengshan Daoist Liu Xuanjing was made Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and an academician of the Hall of Venerating Mystery, granted the style Master Guangcheng. The Hall of Venerating Mystery was furnished for him, with officials appointed and a seal cast.

sentences.zh: 玄靜固辭，乞還山，許之。

translations.literal: Xuanjing firmly declined, begging to return to the mountains; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanjing firmly declined and begged to return to the mountains. His request was granted.

sentences.zh: 李德裕秉政日久，好徇愛憎，人多怨之。

translations.literal: Li Deyu had held power for a long time and liked to indulge his likes and dislikes; many resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu had held power for a long time and indulged his personal likes and dislikes. Many resented him.

sentences.zh: 自杜悰、崔鉉罷相，宦官左右言其太專，上亦不悅。

translations.literal: Since Du Cong and Cui Xuan were removed as chancellors, eunuchs at the emperor's side said that Deyu was too monopolistic, and the emperor was also displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Since Du Cong and Cui Xuan had been removed as chancellors, eunuchs at the emperor's side had said that Deyu was too domineering, and the emperor was displeased as well.

sentences.zh: 給事中韋弘質上疏，言宰相權重，不應更領三司錢穀。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Wei Hongzhi submitted a memorial saying that the chancellor's authority was already heavy and he ought not additionally oversee the three bureaus' funds and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Wei Hongzhi submitted a memorial arguing that the chancellor's authority was already weighty enough and that he should not also oversee the three bureaus' funds and grain.

sentences.zh: 德裕奏稱：「制置職業，人主之柄。

translations.literal: Deyu memorialized, saying: "The establishment and assignment of offices and duties is the sovereign's prerogative.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu memorialized in reply: "The establishment and assignment of offices is the sovereign's prerogative.

sentences.zh: 弘質受人教導，所謂賤人圖柄臣，非所宜言。」

translations.literal: Hongzhi has been tutored by others—what is called a base man plotting against a minister holding power—and this is not language that ought to be spoken."
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi has been coached by others—what the ancients called a base man scheming against a minister in power—and such words ought not be spoken."

sentences.zh: 十二月，弘質坐貶官，由是眾怒愈甚。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Hongzhi was demoted on account of this, and thereby public anger grew all the fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Hongzhi was demoted for this, and public anger only grew fiercer.

sentences.zh: 上自秋冬以來，覺有疾，而道士以為換骨。

translations.literal: Since autumn and winter the emperor had felt illness, but the Daoists held it to be the replacement of bones.
translations.idiomatic: Since autumn the emperor had felt unwell, but the Daoists told him it was the transformation of his bones—a sign the elixir was working.

sentences.zh: 上秘其事，外人但怪上希復遊獵，宰相奏事者亦不敢久留。

translations.literal: The emperor kept the matter secret; outsiders only wondered that the emperor seldom went hunting again, and chancellors presenting memorials also did not dare stay long.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor kept the matter secret. Outsiders only noticed that he seldom went hunting anymore, and chancellors presenting memorials did not dare linger.

sentences.zh: 詔罷來年正旦朝會。

translations.literal: An edict canceled the New Year's Day court assembly for the coming year.
translations.idiomatic: An edict canceled the New Year's Day court assembly for the coming year.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃論恐熱復糾合諸部擊尚婢婢，婢婢遣厖結藏將兵五千拒之，恐熱大敗，與數十騎遁去。

translations.literal: The Tibetan Lun Dore again rallied the various tribes to attack Shang Bibi; Bibi dispatched Mangjizang to lead five thousand troops to resist him. Dore was greatly defeated and fled away with several dozen horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan Lun Dore again rallied the tribes to attack Shang Bibi. Bibi dispatched Mangjizang with five thousand troops to resist him. Dore was routed and fled with only a few dozen horsemen.

sentences.zh: 婢婢傳檄河、湟，數恐熱殘虐之罪，曰：「汝輩本唐人，吐蕃無主，則相與歸唐，毋為恐熱所獵如狐兔也！」

translations.literal: Bibi circulated a proclamation through the He and Huang regions, enumerating Dore's crimes of cruelty and violence, saying: "You were originally men of Tang. If Tibet has no master, then together return to Tang—do not let yourselves be hunted like foxes and hares by Dore!"
translations.idiomatic: Bibi circulated a proclamation through the He and Huang regions, listing Dore's crimes of cruelty and violence. It read: "You were originally men of Tang. If Tibet has no master, then come back to Tang together. Do not let yourselves be hunted like foxes and hares by Dore!"

sentences.zh: 於是諸部從恐熱者稍稍引去。

translations.literal: Thereupon the various tribes that had followed Dore gradually withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the tribes that had followed Dore gradually peeled away.

sentences.zh: 是歲，天下戶四百九十五萬五千一百五十一。

translations.literal: That year, households throughout the realm numbered four million nine hundred fifty-five thousand one hundred fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: That year, registered households throughout the realm numbered four million nine hundred fifty-five thousand one hundred fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 朝廷雖為党項置使，党項侵盜不已，攻陷邠、寧、鹽州界城堡，屯叱利寨。

translations.literal: Although the court had established commissioners for the Tangut, the Tangut continued raiding and plundering without cease, capturing fortresses on the borders of Bin, Ning, and Yan Prefectures and encamping at Chilizhai.
translations.idiomatic: Although the court had appointed commissioners for the Tangut, the Tangut kept raiding without cease, capturing border fortresses in Bin, Ning, and Yan Prefectures and encamping at Chilizhai.

sentences.zh: 宰相請遣使宣慰，上決意討之。

translations.literal: The chancellors requested that envoys be dispatched to offer reassurance; the emperor was resolved to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellors asked that envoys be sent to offer reassurance, but the emperor was resolved to campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 武宗至道昭肅孝皇帝下會昌六年（

translations.literal: Under Emperor Wuzong Zhaosu the Filial, Huichang year 6 (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wuzong, the Filial and Sagely, Huichang year 6 (

sentences.zh: 丙寅，公元八四六年）

translations.literal: bingyin, CE 846)
translations.idiomatic: bingyin, 846 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，二月，庚辰，以夏州節度使米暨為東北道招討党項使。

translations.literal: Spring, second month, on gengchen, Mi Ji, Military Governor of Xia Prefecture, was made Commissioner for Campaigning against the Tangut on the Northeast Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on gengchen of the second month, Mi Ji, military governor of Xia Prefecture, was appointed commissioner for campaigning against the Tangut on the Northeast Circuit.

sentences.zh: 上疾久未平，以為漢火德，改「洛」為「雒」。

translations.literal: The emperor's illness had long gone unremedied. Holding that Han possessed the virtue of Fire, he changed the character for "Luo" in Luoyang from the water radical form to the bird radical form.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's illness continued for a long time without improvement. On the grounds that Han possessed the virtue of Fire, he ordered the place-name character for Luoyang changed from the water-radical form to the bird-radical form.

sentences.zh: 唐土德，不可以王氣勝君名。

translations.literal: Tang possessed the virtue of Earth; the imperial aura of the capital must not be allowed to overpower the sovereign's personal name.
translations.idiomatic: Since Tang possessed the virtue of Earth, the imperial aura associated with the capital's name must not be permitted to clash with the sovereign's own name.

sentences.zh: 三月，下詔改名炎。

translations.literal: In the third month, an edict was issued changing his name to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, an edict was issued changing his name to Yan.

sentences.zh: 上自正月乙卯不視朝，宰相請見，不許。

translations.literal: From the day yimao in the first month the emperor ceased holding court. The chief ministers requested an audience; he refused.
translations.idiomatic: From the day yimao in the first month, the emperor ceased holding court. The chief ministers requested an audience, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 中外憂懼。

translations.literal: Court and countryside alike were anxious and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Court and countryside alike were gripped by anxiety and fear.

sentences.zh: 初，憲宗納李錡妾鄭氏，生光王怡。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Xianzong took as consort Zheng, a concubine of Li Qi, who bore the Prince of Light, Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Xianzong took Zheng, a concubine of Li Qi, as his consort. She bore the Prince of Light, Yi.

sentences.zh: 怡幼時，宮中皆以為不慧，太和以後，益自韜匿，群居游處，未嘗發言。

translations.literal: When Yi was young, everyone in the palace regarded him as dull-witted. After the Taihe era he hid himself all the more; amid group gatherings and amusements he never spoke.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi was young, everyone in the palace regarded him as dull-witted. After the Taihe era he concealed himself all the more, and amid group gatherings and amusements he never spoke.

sentences.zh: 文宗幸十六宅宴集，好誘其言以為戲笑，號曰光叔。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong visited the Sixteen Mansions for feasts, he liked to coax speech from him for sport and mockery, calling him Uncle Light.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong visited the Sixteen Mansions for feasts, he liked to coax words from him for sport and mockery, calling him Uncle Light.

sentences.zh: 上性豪邁，尤所不禮。

translations.literal: The emperor was bold and unrestrained by nature and showed Yi least courtesy of all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was bold and unrestrained by nature and showed Yi the least courtesy of all.

sentences.zh: 及上疾篤，旬日不能言。

translations.literal: When the emperor's illness became grave, for ten days he could not speak.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor's illness became grave, he went ten days without speaking.

sentences.zh: 諸宦官密於禁中定策，辛酉，下詔稱：「皇子沖幼，須選賢德，光王怡可立為皇太叔，更名忱，應軍國政事令權句當。」

translations.literal: The eunuchs secretly settled succession within the forbidden precincts. On xinyou, an edict proclaimed: "The crown prince is still young and requires someone of worthy virtue. The Prince of Light Yi may be established as Imperial Grand Uncle, renamed Chen, and ordered provisionally to oversee all military and state affairs."
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs secretly settled the succession within the forbidden precincts. On xinyou, an edict proclaimed: "The crown prince is still young and requires someone of worthy virtue. The Prince of Light Yi may be established as Imperial Grand Uncle, renamed Chen, and ordered provisionally to oversee all military and state affairs."

sentences.zh: 太叔見百官，哀戚滿容；

translations.literal: The Grand Uncle received the officials, his face full of grief and sorrow;
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Uncle received the officials, his face was full of grief and sorrow;

sentences.zh: 裁決庶務，咸當於理，人始知有隱德焉。

translations.literal: in deciding ordinary affairs, all were handled according to reason, and people first learned that he possessed hidden virtue.
translations.idiomatic: in deciding ordinary affairs, he handled everything according to reason, and people first learned that he possessed hidden virtue.

sentences.zh: 甲子，上崩。

translations.literal: On jiazi, the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 以李德裕攝塚宰。

translations.literal: Li Deyu was appointed acting chief mourner.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu was appointed acting chief mourner.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，宣宗即位。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Emperor Xuanzong took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Emperor Xuanzong took the throne.

sentences.zh: 宣宗素惡李德裕之專，即位之日，德裕奉冊。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong had long disliked Li Deyu's dominance. On the day of enthronement, Deyu presented the succession patent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong had long disliked Li Deyu's dominance. On the day of his enthronement, Deyu presented the succession patent.

sentences.zh: 既罷，謂左右曰：「適近我者非太尉邪？

translations.literal: When it was finished, he said to those beside him: "Was that not the Grand Commandant who just came near me?
translations.idiomatic: When the ceremony was finished, he said to those beside him: "Was that not the Grand Commandant who just came near me?

sentences.zh: 每顧我，使我毛髮灑淅。」

translations.literal: Every time he glanced at me, he made the hair on my body stand on end."
translations.idiomatic: Every time he glanced at me, he made the hair on my body stand on end."

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，辛未朔，上始聽政。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on xinwei the first day of the month, the emperor began to hear government.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on xinwei the first day of the month, the emperor began to hold court.

sentences.zh: 尊母鄭氏為皇太后。

translations.literal: He honored his mother Lady Zheng as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: He honored his mother Lady Zheng as Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 壬申，以門下侍郎、同平章事李德裕同平章事，充荊南節度使。

translations.literal: On renshen, Li Deyu, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Director of the Chancellery, was retained as Associate Director of the Chancellery and made military governor of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Li Deyu, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Director of the Chancellery, was retained as Associate Director of the Chancellery and made military governor of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 德裕秉權日久，位重有功，眾不謂其遽罷，聞之莫不驚駭。

translations.literal: Deyu had held power for a long time; his position was weighty and his achievements great. No one expected him to be so suddenly dismissed, and at the news all were astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu had held power for a long time, his position was weighty and his achievements great. No one expected him to be dismissed so suddenly, and at the news all were astonished.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，貶工部尚書、判鹽鐵轉運使薛元賞為忠州刺史，弟京兆少尹、權知府事元龜為崖州司戶，皆德裕之黨也。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Xue Yuanshang, Minister of Works and Commissioner of Salt and Iron Transport, was demoted to prefect of Zhong Prefecture, and his younger brother Yuangui, Junior Vice Prefect of the Capital District and acting prefect, was demoted to registrar of Ya Prefecture — all were partisans of Deyu.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Xue Yuanshang, Minister of Works and Commissioner of Salt and Iron Transport, was demoted to prefect of Zhong Prefecture, and his younger brother Yuangui, Junior Vice Prefect of the Capital District and acting prefect, was demoted to registrar of Ya Prefecture. All were partisans of Deyu.

sentences.zh: 杖殺道士趙歸真等數人，流羅浮山人軒轅集於嶺南。

translations.literal: Several Daoist priests including Zhao Guizhen were beaten to death, and Xuanyuan Ji of Mount Luofu was exiled to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Several Daoist priests including Zhao Guizhen were beaten to death, and Xuanyuan Ji of Mount Luofu was exiled to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 五月，乙巳，赦天下。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on yisi, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on yisi, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 上京兩街先聽留兩寺外，更各增置八寺；

translations.literal: In the two avenues of the capital, besides the two monasteries previously permitted to remain, eight more were additionally established on each side;
translations.idiomatic: In the two avenues of the capital, besides the two monasteries previously permitted to remain, eight more were established on each side;

sentences.zh: 僧、尼依前隸功德使，不隸主客，所度僧、尼仍令祠部給牒。

translations.literal: monks and nuns as before were placed under the Merit Commissioner, not under the Ministry of Receptions; newly ordained monks and nuns were still ordered to receive certificates from the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: monks and nuns were again placed under the Merit Commissioner rather than the Ministry of Receptions, and newly ordained monks and nuns were still ordered to receive certificates from the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 以翰林學士、兵部侍郎白敏中同平章事。

translations.literal: Bai Minzhong, Academician of the Hanlin Academy and Vice Minister of War, was made Associate Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Minzhong, Academician of the Hanlin Academy and Vice Minister of War, was made Associate Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，立皇子溫為鄆王，水美為雍王，涇為雅王，滋為夔王，沂為慶王。

translations.literal: On xinyou, the emperor's son Wen was made Prince of Yan, Shuimei Prince of Yong, Jing Prince of Ya, Zi Prince of Kui, and Yi Prince of Qing.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, the emperor's son Wen was made Prince of Yan, Shuimei Prince of Yong, Jing Prince of Ya, Zi Prince of Kui, and Yi Prince of Qing.

sentences.zh: 六月，禮儀使奏「請復代宗神主於太廟，以敬宗、文宗、武宗同為一代，於廟東增置兩室，為九代十一室。」

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the Commissioner of Ritual reported: "We request restoring Emperor Daizong's spirit tablet in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, treating Emperors Jingzong, Wenzong, and Wuzong as a single generation, adding two chambers on the east side of the temple, making nine generations and eleven chambers."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, the Commissioner of Ritual reported: "We request restoring Emperor Daizong's spirit tablet in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, treating Emperors Jingzong, Wenzong, and Wuzong as a single generation, adding two chambers on the east side of the temple, for nine generations and eleven chambers in all."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，壬寅，淮南節度使李紳薨。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on renyin, Li Shen, military governor of Huainan, died.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on renyin, Li Shen, military governor of Huainan, died.

sentences.zh: 回鶻烏介可汗之眾稍稍降散及凍餒死，所餘不及三千人。

translations.literal: The forces of the Uyghur Khan Wujie gradually surrendered and dispersed, or died of cold and starvation; those remaining numbered fewer than three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The forces of the Uyghur Khan Wujie gradually surrendered and dispersed, or died of cold and starvation. Those remaining numbered fewer than three thousand.

sentences.zh: 國相逸隱啜殺烏介於金山，立其弟特勒捻為可汗。

translations.literal: The national chancellor Yiyinchuo killed Wujie at Jin Mountain and established his younger brother Tele Nian as khan.
translations.idiomatic: The national chancellor Yiyinchuo killed Wujie at Jin Mountain and established his younger brother Tele Nian as khan.

sentences.zh: 八月，壬申，葬至道昭肅孝皇帝於端陵，廟號武宗。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on renshen, the Zhi-dao Zhaosu Filial Emperor was buried at Duan Mausoleum; his temple name was Wuzong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on renshen, the Zhi-dao Zhaosu Filial Emperor was buried at Duan Mausoleum. His temple name was Wuzong.

sentences.zh: 初，武宗疾困，顧王才人曰：「我死，汝當如何？」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wuzong's illness was critical, he turned to the Talented Lady Wang and said: "When I die, what will you do?"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Wuzong's illness was critical, he turned to the Talented Lady Wang and said: "When I die, what will you do?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「願從陛下於九泉！」

translations.literal: She replied: "I wish to follow Your Majesty to the Nine Springs!"
translations.idiomatic: She replied: "I wish to follow Your Majesty to the Nine Springs!"

sentences.zh: 武宗以巾授之。

translations.literal: Wuzong handed her a scarf.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong handed her a scarf.

sentences.zh: 武宗崩，才人即縊。

translations.literal: When Wuzong died, the Talented Lady immediately hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong died, the Talented Lady immediately hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 上聞而矜之，贈貴妃，葬於端陵柏城之內。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and took pity on her; she was posthumously ennobled as Honored Consort and buried within the cypress precinct of Duan Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it, he took pity on her. She was posthumously ennobled as Honored Consort and buried within the cypress precinct of Duan Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 以循州司馬牛僧孺為衡州長史，封州流人李宗閔為郴州司馬，恩州司馬崔珙為安州長史，潮州刺史楊嗣復為江州刺史，昭州刺史李玨為郴州刺史。

translations.literal: Niu Sengru, army administrator of Xun Prefecture, was made senior administrator of Heng Prefecture; Li Zongmin, exile in Feng Prefecture, was made army administrator of Chen Prefecture; Cui Gong, army administrator of En Prefecture, was made senior administrator of An Prefecture; Yang Sifu, prefect of Chao Prefecture, was made prefect of Jiang Prefecture; Li Jue, prefect of Zhao Prefecture, was made prefect of Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Sengru, army administrator of Xun Prefecture, was made senior administrator of Heng Prefecture; Li Zongmin, an exile in Feng Prefecture, was made army administrator of Chen Prefecture; Cui Gong, army administrator of En Prefecture, was made senior administrator of An Prefecture; Yang Sifu, prefect of Chao Prefecture, was made prefect of Jiang Prefecture; and Li Jue, prefect of Zhao Prefecture, was made prefect of Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 僧孺等五相皆武宗所貶逐，至是，同日北遷。

translations.literal: All five of these chief ministers had been demoted and banished by Wuzong; now on the same day they were transferred northward.
translations.idiomatic: All five of these chief ministers had been demoted and banished by Wuzong. Now, on the same day, they were transferred northward.

sentences.zh: 宗閔未離封州而卒。

translations.literal: Zongmin died before leaving Feng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zongmin died before he could leave Feng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 九月，以荊南節度使李德裕為東都留守，解平章事；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Li Deyu, military governor of Jingnan, was made keeper of the Eastern Capital and relieved of his chancellorship;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Li Deyu, military governor of Jingnan, was made keeper of the Eastern Capital and relieved of his chancellorship;

sentences.zh: 以中書侍郎、同平章事鄭肅同平章事，充荊南節度使。

translations.literal: Zheng Su, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Director of the Chancellery, was retained as Associate Director and made military governor of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Su, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Director of the Chancellery, was retained as Associate Director and made military governor of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 以兵部侍郎、判度支盧商為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Lu Shang, Vice Minister of War and Commissioner of the Treasury, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shang, Vice Minister of War and Commissioner of the Treasury, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 商，翰之族孫也。

translations.literal: Shang was a clansman descendant of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Shang was a clansman descendant of Han.

sentences.zh: 冊黠戛斯可汗使者以國喪未行，或以為僻遠小國，不足與之抗衡。

translations.literal: The envoy to invest the Kirghiz khan did not depart because of the state mourning. Some held that this remote petty state was not worth treating as an equal rival.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy to invest the Kirghiz khan did not depart because of the state mourning. Some held that this remote petty state was not worth treating as an equal rival.

sentences.zh: 回鶻未平，不應遽有建置。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs were not yet settled; there should not be such hasty institutions.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs were not yet settled, and such hasty arrangements should not be made.

sentences.zh: 詔百官集議，事遂寢。

translations.literal: An edict ordered officials of all ranks to assemble and discuss; the matter was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered officials of all ranks to assemble and discuss the matter, and it was then dropped.

sentences.zh: 蠻寇安南，經略使裴元裕帥鄰道兵討之。

translations.literal: The barbarians raided Annam; Military Commissioner Pei Yuanyu led troops from neighboring circuits to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians raided Annam. Military Commissioner Pei Yuanyu led troops from neighboring circuits to attack them.

sentences.zh: 以右常侍李景讓為浙西觀察使。

translations.literal: Li Jingrang was made inspector of Zhexi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jingrang was made inspector of Zhexi.

sentences.zh: 初，景讓母鄭氏，性嚴明，早寡，家貧，居於東都。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jingrang's mother Lady Zheng was strict and clear-minded by nature, widowed early, poor in means, and living in the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Jingrang's mother Lady Zheng was strict and clear-minded by nature. Widowed early and poor in means, she lived in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 諸子皆幼，母自教之。

translations.literal: All her sons were young; the mother taught them herself.
translations.idiomatic: All her sons were still young, and the mother taught them herself.

sentences.zh: 宅後古牆因雨隤陷，得錢盈船，奴婢喜，走告母。

translations.literal: The ancient wall behind the house collapsed in the rain, revealing money enough to fill a boat. The servants rejoiced and ran to tell the mother.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient wall behind the house collapsed in the rain, revealing money enough to fill a boat. The servants rejoiced and ran to tell the mother.

sentences.zh: 母往，焚香祝之曰：「吾聞無勞而獲，身之災也。

translations.literal: The mother went, burned incense, and prayed: "I have heard that gain without labor is a disaster for the person.
translations.idiomatic: The mother went, burned incense, and prayed: "I have heard that gain without labor is a disaster for the person.

sentences.zh: 天必以先君餘慶，矜其貧而賜之，則願諸孤它日學問有成，乃其志也，此不敢取！」

translations.literal: Heaven must be showing pity for our poverty through my late husband's remaining blessings in granting this — then may it be that these orphans one day achieve success in learning; that is my aspiration. This I dare not take!"
translations.idiomatic: Heaven must be showing pity for our poverty through my late husband's remaining blessings in granting this — then may these orphans one day achieve success in learning; that is my aspiration. This I dare not take!"

sentences.zh: 遽命掩而築之。

translations.literal: She immediately ordered it covered and the wall rebuilt.
translations.idiomatic: She immediately ordered it covered and the wall rebuilt.

sentences.zh: 三子景讓、景溫、景莊，皆舉進士及第。

translations.literal: Her three sons Jingrang, Jingwen, and Jingzhuang all passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Her three sons Jingrang, Jingwen, and Jingzhuang all passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 景讓官達，發已斑白，小有過，不免捶楚。

translations.literal: Jingrang rose high in office; though his hair was already streaked with gray, for the smallest fault he still received no exemption from beating.
translations.idiomatic: Jingrang rose high in office, but though his hair was already streaked with gray, for the smallest fault he still received no exemption from beating.

sentences.zh: 景讓在浙西，有左都押牙迕景讓意，景讓杖之而斃。

translations.literal: When Jingrang was in Zhexi, a left chief adjutant displeased him; Jingrang beat him with a staff until he died.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingrang was in Zhexi, a left chief adjutant displeased him. Jingrang beat him with a staff until he died.

sentences.zh: 軍中憤怒，將為變。

translations.literal: The army was outraged and was about to mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: The army was outraged and was about to mutiny.

sentences.zh: 母聞之，景讓方視事，母出坐聽事，立景讓於庭而責之曰：「天子付汝以方面，國家刑法，豈得以為汝喜怒之資，妄殺無罪之人乎！

translations.literal: When the mother heard, Jingrang was just conducting business. The mother came out and sat in the hall of audience, made Jingrang stand in the courtyard, and rebuked him: "The Son of Heaven entrusted you with a frontier command; the laws of the state — can they serve as resources for your whims, to kill innocent people without cause?
translations.idiomatic: When the mother heard, Jingrang was just conducting business. The mother came out and sat in the hall of audience, made Jingrang stand in the courtyard, and rebuked him: "The Son of Heaven entrusted you with a frontier command. Can the laws of the state serve as resources for your whims, to kill innocent people without cause?

sentences.zh: 萬一致一方不寧，豈惟上負朝廷，使垂年之母銜羞入地，何以見汝之先人乎！

translations.literal: If by any chance you unsettle the region, would you not fail the court above and make your aged mother die in shame — how then could you face your ancestors?
translations.idiomatic: If by any chance you unsettle the region, would you not fail the court above and make your aged mother die in shame? How then could you face your ancestors?

sentences.zh: 命左右褫其衣坐之，將撻其背。

translations.literal: She ordered attendants to strip his clothes and seat him, intending to flog his back.
translations.idiomatic: She ordered attendants to strip his clothes and seat him, intending to flog his back.

sentences.zh: 將佐皆為之請，拜且泣，久乃釋之，軍中由是遂安。

translations.literal: The staff all pleaded for him, bowing and weeping; only after a long time was he released, and the army was thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The staff all pleaded for him, bowing and weeping. Only after a long time was he released, and the army was thereby pacified.

sentences.zh: 景莊老於場屋，每被黜，母輒撻景讓。

translations.literal: Jingzhuang grew old in the examination halls; each time he failed, his mother would beat Jingrang.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhuang grew old in the examination halls, and each time he failed, his mother would beat Jingrang.

sentences.zh: 然景讓終不肯屬主司，曰：「朝廷取士自有公道，豈敢效人求關節乎！」

translations.literal: Yet Jingrang would never entreat the examiners, saying: "The court selects scholars by its own fair standard — how dare I imitate others in seeking backdoor connections!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jingrang would never entreat the examiners, saying: "The court selects scholars by its own fair standard — how dare I imitate others in seeking backdoor connections!"

sentences.zh: 久之，宰相謂主司曰：「李景莊今歲不可不收，可憐彼翁每歲受撻！」

translations.literal: After a long time, a chief minister told the examiners: "Li Jingzhuang must be passed this year — pity that old man who takes a beating every year!"
translations.idiomatic: After a long time, a chief minister told the examiners: "Li Jingzhuang must be passed this year — pity that old man who takes a beating every year!"

sentences.zh: 由是始及第。

translations.literal: Thereby Jingzhuang at last passed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereby Jingzhuang at last passed.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，禮院奏禘祭祝文於穆、敬、文、武四室，但稱「嗣皇帝臣某昭告」，從之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, the Board of Ritual reported that in the di-sacrifice prayer texts for the chambers of Mu, Jing, Wen, and Wu, only "the succeeding emperor, your subject So-and-so, announces" should be used. The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, the Board of Ritual reported that in the di-sacrifice prayer texts for the chambers of Mu, Jing, Wen, and Wu, only "the succeeding emperor, your subject So-and-so, announces" should be used. The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 甲申，上受三洞法於菉衡山道士劉玄靜。

translations.literal: On jiashen, the emperor received the Three Caverns teachings from Daoist Liu Xuanjing of Mount Luheng.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, the emperor received the Three Caverns teachings from the Daoist Liu Xuanjing of Mount Luheng.

sentences.zh: 十二月，戊辰朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on wuchen the first day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on wuchen the first day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 宣宗元聖至明成武獻文睿智章仁神聰懿道大孝皇帝上

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong Yuan Sheng Zhi Ming Cheng Wu Xian Wen Rui Zhi Zhang Ren Shen Cong Yi Dao Da Xiao, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong Yuan Sheng Zhi Ming Cheng Wu Xian Wen Rui Zhi Zhang Ren Shen Cong Yi Dao Da Xiao, Part One

sentences.zh: 宣宗至道昭肅孝皇帝下大中元年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong Zhi-dao Zhao Su the Filial, Part Two, Dazhong year 1 (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong Zhi-dao Zhao Su the Filial, Part Two, Dazhong year 1 (

sentences.zh: 丁卯，公元八四七年）

translations.literal: dingmao, CE 847)
translations.idiomatic: dingmao, CE 847)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲寅，上祀圓丘，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on jiayin, the emperor sacrificed at the Round Altar, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the reign era.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on jiayin, the emperor sacrificed at the Round Altar, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the reign era.

sentences.zh: 二月，庚午，加盧龍節度使張仲武同平章事，賞其屢破回鶻也。

translations.literal: In the second month, on gengwu, Zhang Zhongwu, military governor of Lulong, was granted the title Associate Director of the Chancellery, rewarding his repeated defeats of the Uyghurs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on gengwu, Zhang Zhongwu, military governor of Lulong, was granted the title Associate Director of the Chancellery, rewarding his repeated defeats of the Uyghurs.

sentences.zh: 癸未，上以旱故，減膳徹樂，出宮女，縱鷹隼，止營繕，命中書侍郎、同平章事盧商與御史中丞封敖疏理京城系囚。

translations.literal: On guimei, because of drought the emperor reduced his meals, removed music, released palace women, freed hawks and falcons, halted construction, and ordered Lu Shang, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Director of the Chancellery, and Supervisory Censor-in-Chief Feng Ao to review prisoners held in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On guimei, because of drought the emperor reduced his meals, removed music, released palace women, freed hawks and falcons, halted construction, and ordered Lu Shang, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Director of the Chancellery, and Supervisory Censor-in-Chief Feng Ao to review prisoners held in the capital.

sentences.zh: 大理卿馬植奏稱：「盧商等務行寬宥，凡抵極法者，一切免死。

translations.literal: Court of Judicial Review Director Ma Zhi memorialized: "Lu Shang and others are bent on leniency; all who had merited the extreme penalty are entirely spared death.
translations.idiomatic: Court of Judicial Review Director Ma Zhi memorialized: "Lu Shang and others are bent on leniency. All who had merited the extreme penalty are entirely spared death.

sentences.zh: 彼官典犯贓及故殺人，平日大赦所不免，今因疏理而原之，使貪吏無所懲畏，死者銜冤無告，恐非所以消旱災、致和氣也。

translations.literal: Those guilty officials of embezzlement and deliberate murder — whom even ordinary great amnesties do not exempt — are now pardoned through this review. This leaves corrupt officials with nothing to fear and the dead to bear grudges with none to hear them. I fear this is not the way to dispel drought disaster and summon harmonious qi.
translations.idiomatic: Those guilty officials of embezzlement and deliberate murder — whom even ordinary great amnesties do not exempt — are now pardoned through this review. This leaves corrupt officials with nothing to fear and the dead to bear grudges with none to hear them. I fear this is not the way to dispel drought disaster and summon harmonious qi.

sentences.zh: 昔周饑，克殷而年豐；

translations.literal: In antiquity when Zhou suffered famine, they conquered Yin and the year was bountiful;
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when Zhou suffered famine, they conquered Yin and the year was bountiful;

sentences.zh: 衛旱，討邢而雨降。

translations.literal: when Wei suffered drought, they chastised Xing and rain fell.
translations.idiomatic: when Wei suffered drought, they chastised Xing and rain fell.

sentences.zh: 是則誅罪戮奸，式合天意，雪冤決滯，乃副聖心也。

translations.literal: Thus punishing crimes and executing the wicked accords with Heaven's intent; clearing wrongs and resolving stale cases fulfills the sage heart.
translations.idiomatic: Thus punishing crimes and executing the wicked accords with Heaven's intent, and clearing wrongs and resolving stale cases fulfills the sage heart.

sentences.zh: 乞再加裁定。」

translations.literal: I beg that further judgment be applied."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that further judgment be applied."

sentences.zh: 詔兩省五品以上議之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered officials of fifth rank and above in both secretariats to discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered officials of fifth rank and above in both secretariats to discuss it.

sentences.zh: 初，李德裕執政，引白敏中為翰林學士。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Li Deyu held the government, he brought in Bai Minzhong as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Li Deyu held the government, he brought in Bai Minzhong as Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 乃武宗崩，德裕失勢，敏中乘上下之怒，竭力排之，使其黨李鹹訟德裕罪，德裕由是自東都留守以太子少保、分司。

translations.literal: When Wuzong died and Deyu lost power, Minzhong seized on the anger of sovereign and court, exerted himself to drive Deyu out, had his partisan Li Xian impeach Deyu, and Deyu was thus moved from keeper of the Eastern Capital to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent with a post outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong died and Deyu lost power, Minzhong seized on the anger of sovereign and court, exerted himself to drive Deyu out, had his partisan Li Xian impeach Deyu, and Deyu was thus moved from keeper of the Eastern Capital to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent with a post outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 左諫議大夫張鷺等上言：「陛下以旱理系囚，慮有冤滯。

translations.literal: Left Remonstrance Grandee Zhang Lu and others submitted: "Your Majesty reviewed prisoners held because of drought, fearing there were wrongs unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: Left Remonstrance Grandee Zhang Lu and others submitted: "Your Majesty reviewed prisoners held because of drought, fearing there were wrongs unresolved.

sentences.zh: 今所原死罪，無冤可雪，恐凶險僥倖之徒常思水旱為災，宜如馬植所奏。」

translations.literal: Those now pardoned from death sentences have no wrongs to clear; I fear that vicious and opportunistic men will always hope drought and flood bring disaster. The court should follow Ma Zhi's memorial."
translations.idiomatic: Those now pardoned from death sentences have no wrongs to clear. I fear that vicious and opportunistic men will always hope drought and flood bring disaster. The court should follow Ma Zhi's memorial."

sentences.zh: 詔從之，皆論如法。

translations.literal: The edict accepted this; all were sentenced according to law.
translations.idiomatic: The edict accepted this, and all were sentenced according to law.

sentences.zh: 以植為刑部侍郎，充鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: Ma Zhi was made Vice Minister of Justice and Commissioner of Salt and Iron Transport.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhi was made Vice Minister of Justice and Commissioner of Salt and Iron Transport.

sentences.zh: 植素以文學政事有名於時，李德裕不之重。

translations.literal: Ma Zhi had long been renowned in his day for literary and administrative talent; Li Deyu did not hold him in high regard.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhi had long been renowned in his day for literary and administrative talent, but Li Deyu did not hold him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 及白敏中秉政，凡德裕所薄者，皆不次用之。

translations.literal: When Bai Minzhong held power, all whom Deyu had slighted were promoted out of turn.
translations.idiomatic: When Bai Minzhong held power, all whom Deyu had slighted were promoted out of turn.

sentences.zh: 以盧商為武昌節度使，以刑部尚書、判度支崔元式為門下侍郎，翰林學士、戶部侍郎韋琮為中書侍郎，並同平章事。

translations.literal: Lu Shang was made military governor of Wuchang; Cui Yuanshi, Minister of Justice and Commissioner of the Treasury, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat; Wei Cong, Hanlin Academician and Vice Minister of Revenue, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat — all as Associate Directors of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shang was made military governor of Wuchang; Cui Yuanshi, Minister of Justice and Commissioner of the Treasury, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat; and Wei Cong, Hanlin Academician and Vice Minister of Revenue, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat — all as Associate Directors of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 閏三月，敕：「應會昌五年所廢寺，有僧能營葺者，聽自居之，有司毋得禁止。」

translations.literal: In the intercalary third month, an edict: "Of the monasteries abolished in Huichang year 5, wherever monks are able to repair them, let them dwell there; officials must not prohibit it."
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary third month, an edict proclaimed: "Of the monasteries abolished in Huichang year 5, wherever monks are able to repair them, let them dwell there. Officials must not prohibit it."

sentences.zh: 是時君、相務反會昌之政，故僧、尼之弊皆復其舊。

translations.literal: At this time sovereign and chancellor were bent on reversing Huichang policies, so the abuses of monks and nuns all returned to their former state.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the sovereign and chancellor were bent on reversing Huichang policies, so the abuses of monks and nuns all returned to their former state.

sentences.zh: 己酉，積慶太后蕭氏崩。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Empress Dowager Xiao of Jiqing died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Empress Dowager Xiao of Jiqing died.

sentences.zh: 五月，幽州節度使張仲武大破諸奚。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Zhang Zhongwu, military governor of Youzhou, greatly defeated the various Xi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Zhang Zhongwu, military governor of Youzhou, routed the Xi tribes.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃論恐熱乘武宗之喪，誘党項及回鶻餘眾寇河西，詔河東節度使王宰將代北諸軍擊之。

translations.literal: The Tibetan Lun Kongre, seizing upon Wuzong's mourning, incited the Tangut and remnant Uyghur forces to raid Hexi. An edict ordered Wang Zai, military governor of Hedong, to lead the armies of the northern frontier to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan general Lun Kongre took advantage of Emperor Wuzong's death to stir up the Tangut and surviving Uyghurs against Hexi. The court ordered Wang Zai, military governor of Hedong, to march the northern frontier armies against him.

sentences.zh: 宰以沙陀朱邪赤心為前鋒，自麟州濟河，與恐熱戰於鹽州，破走之。

translations.literal: Zai took the Shatuo Zhuo Yicheng as vanguard, crossed the river from Lin Prefecture, fought Kongre at Yan Prefecture, defeated him and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Zai put the Shatuo chieftain Zhuo Yicheng at the head of his column, crossed the Yellow River from Lin Prefecture, met Kongre at Yan Prefecture, and broke his army in flight.

sentences.zh: 六月，以鴻臚卿李業為冊黠戛斯英武誠明可汗使。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Li Ye, Minister of Ceremonies, was appointed envoy to invest the Kirghiz Khan as Khan Yingwu Chengming.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Li Ye, Minister of Ceremonies, was sent as envoy to invest the Kirghiz ruler with the title of Khan Yingwu Chengming.

sentences.zh: 上請白敏中曰：「朕昔從憲宗之喪，道遇風雨，百官、六宮四散避去，惟山陵使長而多髯，攀靈駕不去，誰也？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked Bai Minzhong, saying: "When I once followed Emperor Xianzong's funeral procession, we met wind and rain on the road. The hundred officials and the six palaces scattered in all directions to take shelter. Only the director of the imperial tomb—a tall man with a full beard—clung to the spirit carriage and would not leave. Who was he?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Bai Minzhong: "When I once followed Emperor Xianzong's funeral cortege, a storm struck on the road. Officials and palace women fled in every direction—only one man, tall and bearded, the director of the imperial tomb, clung to the spirit carriage and would not leave. Who was he?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「令狐楚。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Linghu Chu."
translations.idiomatic: Minzhong answered, "Linghu Chu."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「有子乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Does he have sons?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Does he have sons?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「長子緒今為隨州刺史。」

translations.literal: He replied: "The eldest son Xu is now prefect of Suizhou."
translations.idiomatic: "His eldest son Xu is now prefect of Suizhou."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「堪為相乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Is he fit to serve as chancellor?"
translations.idiomatic: "Would he be fit for the chancellorship?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「緒少病風痺。

translations.literal: He replied: "Xu has suffered from wind paralysis since youth.
translations.idiomatic: "Xu has been afflicted with paralysis since he was young.

sentences.zh: 次子綯，前湖州刺史，有才器。」

translations.literal: The second son Tao, former prefect of Huzhou, has talent and ability."
translations.idiomatic: The second son, Tao, formerly prefect of Huzhou, has talent and ability."

sentences.zh: 上即擢為考功郎中、知制誥。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately promoted him to Director of the Bureau of Evaluation and Controller of Drafts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at once promoted Tao to Director of the Bureau of Evaluation and Controller of Drafts.

sentences.zh: 綯入謝，上問以元和故事，綯條對甚悉，上悅，遂有大用之意。

translations.literal: Tao entered to give thanks. The emperor questioned him on precedents from the Yuanhe reign, and Tao answered item by item with great thoroughness. The emperor was pleased and came to intend great employment for him.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao came to give thanks, the emperor tested him on Yuanhe-era precedents. Tao answered point by point with exhaustive detail. The emperor was delighted and began to think of giving him high office.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，丙申，以門下侍郎、同平章事李回同平章事，充西川節度使。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on the day bingshen, Li Hui, Vice Director of the Chancellery and Associate Director of the Chancellery, was confirmed as Associate Director of the Chancellery and made military governor of Xichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, on bingshen, Li Hui—Vice Director of the Chancellery and Associate Director of the Chancellery—was confirmed in the chancellorship and assigned as military governor of Xichuan.

sentences.zh: 葬貞獻皇后於光陵之側。

translations.literal: Empress Zhenxian was buried beside Guang Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhenxian was buried beside Emperor Xianzong's Guang Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 上敦睦兄弟，作雍和殿於十六宅，數臨幸，置酒，作樂，擊球盡歡。

translations.literal: The emperor cultivated harmony among his brothers. He built the Yonghe Hall in the Sixteen Mansions, often visited it, set out wine, had music performed, and played cuju to the full of their pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor cultivated brotherly affection. He built the Yonghe Hall in the princes' Sixteen Mansions, visited often, set out wine, ordered music, and played cuju with them in full merriment.

sentences.zh: 諸王有疾，常親至臥內存問，憂形於色。

translations.literal: When any prince fell ill, he often went in person to the bedside to inquire after him, with worry showing on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a prince fell ill, he would go in person to the sickroom to inquire after him, his face clouded with worry.

sentences.zh: 突厥掠漕米及行商，振武節度使史憲忠擊破之。

translations.literal: The Turks plundered grain transport and traveling merchants. Shi Xianzhong, military governor of Zhenwu, attacked and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Turks raided grain transports and merchant traffic. Shi Xianzhong, military governor of Zhenwu, struck them and broke their force.

sentences.zh: 九月，丁卯，以金吾大將軍鄭光為平盧節度使。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day dingmao, Zheng Guang, Grand General of the Imperial Guard, was made military governor of Pinglu.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on dingmao, Zheng Guang, Grand General of the Imperial Guard, was appointed military governor of Pinglu.

sentences.zh: 光，潤州人，太后之弟也。

translations.literal: Guang was a native of Runzhou and the empress dowager's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Guang was from Runzhou—the empress dowager's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，前永寧尉吳汝納，訟其弟湘罪不至死，「李紳與李德裕相表裡，期罔武宗，枉殺臣弟，乞召江州司戶崔元藻等對辨。」

translations.literal: On yiyou, Wu Runa, former captain of Yongning, sued that his brother Xiang's crime did not merit death: "Li Shen and Li Deyu acted in concert, scheming to deceive Wuzong and unjustly kill my brother. I beg that Cui Yuanzao, registrar of Jiang Prefecture, and others be summoned to confront and argue the matter."
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, Wu Runa, former captain of Yongning, petitioned that his brother Xiang's offense did not warrant death: "Li Shen and Li Deyu worked hand in glove, plotting to mislead Emperor Wuzong and put my brother to death unjustly. I ask that Cui Yuanzao, registrar of Jiang Prefecture, and others be summoned to testify and cross-examine the case."

sentences.zh: 丁亥，敕御史台鞫實以聞。

translations.literal: On dinghai, an edict ordered the Censorate to investigate the facts and report.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, the emperor ordered the Censorate to investigate and report back.

sentences.zh: 冬，十二月，庚戌，御史台奏，據崔元藻所列吳湘冤狀，如吳汝納之言。

translations.literal: In winter, the twelfth month, on the day gengxu, the Censorate memorialized that, according to the account of Wu Xiang's wrongful conviction set forth by Cui Yuanzao, it was as Wu Runa had said.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the twelfth month, on gengxu, the Censorate reported that Cui Yuanzao's account of Wu Xiang's wrongful conviction confirmed Wu Runa's allegations.

sentences.zh: 戊午，貶太子少保、分司李德裕為潮州司馬。

translations.literal: On wuwu, Li Deyu, Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent serving at his post in the eastern capital, was demoted to military adjutant of Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, Li Deyu—Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent on detached duty—was demoted to military adjutant of Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 吏部奏，會昌四年所減州縣官內復增三百八十三員。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel memorialized that among the prefectural and county posts cut in Huichang year 4, three hundred eighty-three positions had been added back.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel reported that three hundred eighty-three of the prefectural and county posts cut in Huichang year 4 had already been restored.

sentences.zh: 宣宗至道昭肅孝皇帝下大中二年（

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xuanzong Zhaosu the Filial, Dazhong year 2 (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong, the Filial and Sagely, Dazhong year 2 (

sentences.zh: 戊辰，公元八四八年）

translations.literal: wuchen, CE 848)
translations.idiomatic: wuchen, 848 CE)

sentences.zh: 正月，甲子，群臣上尊號曰聖敬文思和武光孝皇帝；

translations.literal: In the first month, on the day jiazi, the assembled ministers offered the honorific title Emperor Shengjing Wensi Hewu Guangxiao;
translations.idiomatic: In the first month, on jiazi, the ministers offered the honorific title Emperor Shengjing Wensi Hewu Guangxiao;

sentences.zh: 赦天下。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: and a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 初，李德裕執政，有薦丁柔立清直可任諫官者，德裕不能用。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Li Deyu held power, someone recommended Ding Rouli as upright and fit for service as a remonstrance official, but Deyu did not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Li Deyu was in power, someone recommended Ding Rouli as upright and fit for a remonstrance post, but Deyu would not use him.

sentences.zh: 上即位，柔立為右補闕。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, Rouli was made Right Remonstrance Officer.
translations.idiomatic: When the new emperor took the throne, Rouli was appointed Right Remonstrance Officer.

sentences.zh: 德裕貶潮州，柔立上疏訟其冤。

translations.literal: When Deyu was demoted to Chaozhou, Rouli submitted a memorial pleading his wrongful treatment.
translations.idiomatic: After Deyu was demoted to Chaozhou, Rouli submitted a memorial protesting his unjust treatment.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，坐阿附貶南陽尉。

translations.literal: On bingyin, for the offense of partisan attachment he was demoted to captain of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, for currying favor with the disgraced minister, he was demoted to captain of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 西川節度使李回、桂管觀察使鄭亞坐前不能直吳湘冤，乙酉，回左遷湖南觀察使，亞貶循州刺史，李紳追奪三任告身。

translations.literal: Li Hui, military governor of Xichuan, and Zheng Ya, observation commissioner of Guiguan, were punished for having earlier failed to set right the injustice against Wu Xiang. On yiyou, Hui was transferred to observation commissioner of Hunan, Ya was demoted to prefect of Xunzhou, and Li Shen's commissions for three terms of office were revoked.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hui, military governor of Xichuan, and Zheng Ya, observation commissioner of Guiguan, were punished for failing to redress Wu Xiang's wrongful conviction. On yiyou, Hui was transferred to Hunan as observation commissioner, Ya was demoted to prefect of Xunzhou, and Li Shen's commissions for three past appointments were revoked.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人崔嘏坐草李德裕制不盡言其罪，己丑，貶端州刺史。

translations.literal: Cui Gu, Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat, was punished for drafting Li Deyu's demotion edict without fully stating his crimes. On jichou, he was demoted to prefect of Duanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Gu, Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat, was punished for drafting Li Deyu's demotion edict without fully enumerating his offenses. On jichou, he was demoted to prefect of Duanzhou.

sentences.zh: 回鶻遏捻可汗仰給於奚王石捨朗。

translations.literal: The Uyghur Khan Enian relied for subsistence on the Xi chieftain Shi Sheleng.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghur Khan Enian depended on the Xi chieftain Shi Sheleng for his livelihood.

sentences.zh: 及張仲琥大破奚眾，回鶻無所得食，日益耗散。

translations.literal: When Zhang Zhonghu greatly defeated the Xi masses, the Uyghurs had no food to obtain and daily grew weaker and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Zhonghu routed the Xi, the Uyghurs could no longer find food and dwindled day by day.

sentences.zh: 至是，所存貴臣以下不滿五百人，依於室韋。

translations.literal: By this time, those who remained, from high ministers downward, numbered fewer than five hundred, and they depended on the Shiwei.
translations.idiomatic: By then fewer than five hundred Uyghurs remained, from nobles down to commoners, and they took refuge with the Shiwei.

sentences.zh: 使者入賀正，過幽州，張仲武使歸取遏捻等。

translations.literal: An envoy came to offer New Year's congratulations. Passing through Youzhou, Zhang Zhongwu sent him back to seize Enian and the others.
translations.idiomatic: When an envoy came to offer New Year's greetings and passed through Youzhou, Zhang Zhongwu sent him back to capture Enian and his followers.

sentences.zh: 遏捻聞之，夜與妻葛祿、子特勒毒斯等九騎西走，餘眾追之不及，相與大哭。

translations.literal: When Enian heard of this, he fled west by night with nine riders, including his wife Gelu and his son Teledusi. The remaining masses pursued but could not overtake them, and together they wept aloud.
translations.idiomatic: Enian heard of the plot and fled west by night with nine companions—his wife Gelu, his son Teledusi, and seven others. The rest pursued but could not catch them, and together they broke into loud weeping.

sentences.zh: 室韋分回鶻餘眾為七，七姓共分之。

translations.literal: The Shiwei divided the remaining Uyghur masses into seven groups, and seven clans shared them among themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The Shiwei divided the surviving Uyghurs into seven groups and distributed them among seven clans.

sentences.zh: 居二日，黠戛斯遣其相阿播帥諸胡兵號七萬來取回鶻，大破室韋，悉收回鶻餘眾歸磧北。

translations.literal: After two days, the Kirghiz sent their chancellor A Bo leading various barbarian troops said to number seventy thousand to take the Uyghurs. They greatly defeated the Shiwei and took back all the remaining Uyghur masses to the north of the desert.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later the Kirghiz chancellor A Bo marched with a force said to number seventy thousand to reclaim the Uyghurs. He routed the Shiwei and carried all the surviving Uyghurs back north of the desert.

sentences.zh: 猶有數帳，潛竄山林，鈔盜諸胡。

translations.literal: Still, several encampments hid themselves in mountain forests and plundered the various tribes.
translations.idiomatic: A few bands still lurked in the forests and raided neighboring tribes.

sentences.zh: 其別部厖勒，先在安西，亦自稱可汗，居甘州，總磧西諸城，種落微弱，時入獻見。

translations.literal: Their separate branch under Pang Le, earlier in Anxi, also styled himself khan, dwelt at Gan Prefecture, governed the various cities west of the desert, was weak in numbers, and from time to time came to offer tribute and audience.
translations.idiomatic: A separate Uyghur branch under Pang Le, long settled in Anxi, also styled himself khan. Based at Gan Prefecture, he held sway over the oasis towns west of the desert. His people were few and weak, but he sent tribute and audiences from time to time.

sentences.zh: 二月，庚子，以知制誥令狐綯為翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day gengzi, Linghu Tao, Controller of Drafts, was made Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on gengzi, Linghu Tao, Controller of Drafts, was appointed Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 上嘗以太宗所撰《金鏡》授綯，使讀之，「至亂未嘗不任不肖，至治未嘗不任忠賢，」上止之曰：「凡求致太平，當以此言為首。」

translations.literal: The emperor once gave Tao the Golden Mirror composed by Emperor Taizong and had him read it: "In utmost disorder one never fails to employ the unworthy; in utmost order one never fails to employ the loyal and worthy." The emperor stopped him and said: "In all seeking to attain great peace, this saying should be taken as foremost."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once handed Tao Emperor Taizong's Golden Mirror and had him read aloud: "In ages of chaos, unworthy men are always put in office; in ages of good order, loyal and worthy men always are." The emperor stopped him and said: "Whoever seeks to bring the realm to peace must take that line as his first principle."

sentences.zh: 又書《貞觀政要》於屏風，每正色拱手而讀之。

translations.literal: He also had the Essentials of Government from the Zhenguan Reign written on a screen and, each time, read it with solemn countenance and hands joined in respect.
translations.idiomatic: He also had passages from the Essentials of Government from the Zhenguan Reign copied onto a screen and would read them with grave face and joined hands.

sentences.zh: 上欲知百官名數，令狐`綯曰：「六品已下，官卑數多，皆吏部注擬；

translations.literal: The emperor wished to know the names and numbers of the hundred officials. Linghu Tao said: "For ranks of the sixth grade and below, the posts are lowly and numerous; all are nominated by the Ministry of Personnel;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor wished to know the roster of officials, Linghu Tao said: "For ranks of the sixth grade and below, the posts are humble and numerous—all are nominated by the Ministry of Personnel;

sentences.zh: 五品以上，則政府制授，各有籍，命曰具員。」

translations.literal: for the fifth grade and above, the government appoints by edict. Each has a register, called the Full Establishment."
translations.idiomatic: for the fifth grade and above, appointments come directly from the throne. Each office has a register—the Full Establishment."

sentences.zh: 上命宰相作《具員御覽》五卷，上之，常置於案上。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the chancellors to compile the Imperial Review of the Full Establishment in five scrolls and submit it. He kept it constantly on his desk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the chancellors to compile the Imperial Review of the Full Establishment in five scrolls and submit it. He kept the work on his desk at all times.

sentences.zh: 立皇子澤為濮王。

translations.literal: The emperor's son Ze was established as Prince of Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ze, the emperor's son, was enfeoffed as Prince of Pu.

sentences.zh: 上欲作五王院於大明宮，以處皇子之幼者，召術士柴岳明使相其地。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to build a Court of the Five Princes in Daming Palace to house the younger princes. He summoned the geomancer Chai Yueming to inspect the site.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to build a Court of the Five Princes in Daming Palace for his younger sons. He summoned the geomancer Chai Yueming to survey the site.

sentences.zh: 岳明對曰：「臣庶之家，廷徙不常，故有自陽宅入陰宅，陰宅入陽宅。

translations.literal: Yueming replied: "In the households of subjects, residences change constantly, and so there are moves from the yang dwelling into the yin dwelling, and from the yin dwelling into the yang dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Yueming replied: "Common households move their dwellings often, and so geomancers speak of passing from a yang dwelling into a yin one, and from a yin dwelling back into a yang one.

sentences.zh: 刑克禍福，師有其說，今陛下深拱法宮，萬神擁衛，陰陽書本不言帝王家。」

translations.literal: Calamity, blessing, and the clash of elemental forces—masters have their explanations for these. But Your Majesty deeply withdraws within the palace of law, ten thousand spirits surround and guard you. Books of yin and yang do not speak of the households of emperors."
translations.idiomatic: Masters have their theories about auspice and misfortune, clash and harmony—but Your Majesty sits deep within the palace of law, guarded by ten thousand spirits. The yin-yang texts were never written for imperial households."

sentences.zh: 上善其言，賜束帛遣之。」

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words, gave him silk, and sent him away."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his answer, rewarded him with silk, and dismissed him."

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，己未朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on the first day of the month, jiawei, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, on the first day jiawei, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 門下侍郎、同平章事崔元式罷為戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Cui Yuanshi, Vice Director of the Chancellery and Associate Director of the Chancellery, was removed and made Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuanshi, Vice Director of the Chancellery and Associate Director of the Chancellery, was removed from the chancellorship and made Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 以兵部侍郎、判度支、戶部周墀、刑部侍郎、鹽鐵轉運使馬植並同平章事。

translations.literal: Zhou Chi, Vice Minister of War and acting Commissioner of the Finance and Revenue Commissions, and Ma Zhi, Vice Minister of Justice and Salt and Iron Transport Commissioner, were both made Associate Directors of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chi—Vice Minister of War and acting Commissioner of the Finance and Revenue Commissions—and Ma Zhi—Vice Minister of Justice and Salt and Iron Transport Commissioner—were both appointed Associate Directors of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 初，墀為義成節度使，辟韋澳為判官，及為相，謂澳曰：「力小任重，何以相助？」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chi was military governor of Yicheng, he recruited Wei Ao as administrative aide. When he became chancellor, he said to Ao: "My strength is small and my burden heavy—how can you help me?"
translations.idiomatic: When Chi had been military governor of Yicheng, he had recruited Wei Ao as his administrative aide. After becoming chancellor, he said to Ao: "My strength is slight and my burden great—how can you help me?"

sentences.zh: 澳曰：「願相公無權。」

translations.literal: Ao said: "I wish that the Chancellor would have no power."
translations.idiomatic: Ao said, "I wish you would wield no power at all."

sentences.zh: 墀愕然，不知所措。

translations.literal: Chi was startled and did not know what to make of it.
translations.idiomatic: Chi was stunned and did not know what to say.

sentences.zh: 澳曰：「官賞刑罰，與天下共其可否，勿以己之愛憎喜怒移之，天下自理，何權之有！」

translations.literal: Ao said: "Office, reward, punishment, and penalty should be judged together with the realm as to what is permissible or not. Do not shift them according to your own likes, dislikes, joy, or anger. The realm will govern itself—what power would there be!"
translations.idiomatic: Ao said: "Appointments, rewards, and punishments should be decided with the realm, not shifted by your private likes, dislikes, joy, or anger. Let the realm govern itself—what need is there for power?"

sentences.zh: 墀深然之。

translations.literal: Chi deeply agreed with this.
translations.idiomatic: Chi was deeply convinced.

sentences.zh: 澳，貫之之子也。

translations.literal: Ao was the son of Guanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Ao was the son of Wei Guanzhi.

sentences.zh: 己卯，太皇太后郭氏崩於興慶宮。

translations.literal: On jimao, Grand Empress Dowager Guo died in Xingqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, Grand Empress Dowager Guo died in Xingqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 六月，禮院檢討官王皞貶句容令。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Wang Hao, review officer of the Board of Rites, was demoted to magistrate of Jurong.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Wang Hao, review officer of the Board of Rites, was demoted to magistrate of Jurong.

sentences.zh: 初，憲宗之崩，上疑郭太后預其謀。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xianzong died, the emperor suspected that Empress Dowager Guo had taken part in the plot.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong died, the new emperor had suspected Empress Dowager Guo of complicity in the plot.

sentences.zh: 又，鄭太后本郭太后侍兒，有宿怨，故上即位，待郭太后禮殊薄，郭太后意怏怏。

translations.literal: Moreover, Empress Dowager Zheng had originally been a maid of Empress Dowager Guo, and there was an old grudge between them. Therefore, when the emperor took the throne, he treated Empress Dowager Guo with markedly thin ceremony, and Empress Dowager Guo was resentful.
