translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Zheng had once been a maid in Empress Dowager Guo's service, and the two bore an old grudge. When the new emperor took the throne, he treated Empress Dowager Guo with conspicuous coldness, and she grew deeply resentful.

sentences.zh: 一日，登勤政樓，欲自隕。

translations.literal: One day she ascended the Qinzheng Tower, intending to cast herself down to her death.
translations.idiomatic: One day she climbed the Qinzheng Tower, intending to throw herself to her death.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，大怒，是夕，崩，外人頗有異論。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he was greatly angered. That very night she died, and outsiders had much suspicious talk.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it, he flew into a rage. That very night she died, and many outside the palace whispered darkly about it.

sentences.zh: 上以鄭太后故，不欲以郭后祔憲宗。

translations.literal: Because of Empress Dowager Zheng, the emperor did not wish to have Empress Guo enshrined beside Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Empress Dowager Zheng, the emperor did not wish to have Empress Guo enshrined beside Emperor Xianzong.

sentences.zh: 有司請葬景陵外園，皞奏宜合葬景陵，神主配憲宗室。

translations.literal: The responsible offices requested burial in the outer park of Jing Mausoleum. Hao memorialized that she should be buried jointly in Jing Mausoleum, with her spirit tablet placed in Xianzong's shrine.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices proposed burying her in the outer precinct of Jing Mausoleum. Hao memorialized that she ought to be buried jointly in Jing Mausoleum, with her spirit tablet placed in Emperor Xianzong's shrine.

sentences.zh: 奏入，上大怒。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor was greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, the emperor was furious.

sentences.zh: 白敏中召皞詰之。

translations.literal: Bai Minzhong summoned Hao and interrogated him.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Minzhong summoned Hao and pressed him for an explanation.

sentences.zh: 皞曰：「太皇太后，汾陽王之孫，憲宗在東宮為正妃，逮事順宗為婦。

translations.literal: Hao said: "The Grand Empress Dowager was the granddaughter of the Prince of Fenyang. When Xianzong was in the Eastern Palace she was his principal consort, and she served Emperor Shunzong as his daughter-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said: "The Grand Empress Dowager was a granddaughter of the Prince of Fenyang. When Emperor Xianzong was heir apparent, she was his principal consort, and she served Emperor Shunzong as daughter-in-law.

sentences.zh: 憲宗厭代之夕，事出暖昧。

translations.literal: On the night Xianzong passed from the world, the matter arose in obscurity.
translations.idiomatic: On the night Emperor Xianzong died, the circumstances were murky.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后母天下，歷五朝，豈得以暖昧之事遽廢正嫡之禮乎！」

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager was mother to the realm and passed through five reigns—how can one, on the basis of obscure matters, abruptly abolish the rites due a principal consort!"
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager was mother to the realm and lived through five reigns—how can murky rumors be grounds to deny a principal consort her rightful rites!"

sentences.zh: 敏中怒甚，皞辭氣愈厲。

translations.literal: Minzhong was very angry, and Hao's tone grew ever sharper.
translations.idiomatic: Minzhong grew angrier, but Hao's tone only sharpened.

sentences.zh: 諸相會食，周墀立於敏中之門以俟之。

translations.literal: The chancellors were to dine together. Zhou Chi stood at Minzhong's gate waiting for him.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellors were to dine together. Zhou Chi waited at Minzhong's gate.

sentences.zh: 敏中使謝曰：「方為一書生所苦，公弟先行。」

translations.literal: Minzhong sent word of apology, saying: "I am just now being harried by a mere scholar—Your Excellency, go on ahead."
translations.idiomatic: Minzhong sent word: "I am being harried by a mere scholar—go on ahead without me."

sentences.zh: 墀入，至敏中廳問其事，見皞爭辨方急，墀舉手加顙，歎皞孤直。

translations.literal: Chi entered, went to Minzhong's hall to ask about the matter, saw Hao arguing fiercely, raised his hand to his forehead, and sighed at Hao's solitary uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Chi went in, found Minzhong's hall, and saw Hao still arguing fiercely. Chi raised his hand to his forehead and sighed at the man's lonely integrity.

sentences.zh: 明日，皞坐貶官。

translations.literal: The next day, Hao was demoted for his offense.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Hao was demoted.

sentences.zh: 秋，九月，甲子，再貶潮州司馬李德裕為崖州司戶，湖南觀察使李回為賀州刺史。

translations.literal: In autumn, the ninth month, on the day jiazi, Li Deyu, military adjutant of Chaozhou, was again demoted to registrar of Yazhou, and Li Hui, observation commissioner of Hunan, was demoted to prefect of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the ninth month, on jiazi, Li Deyu—already demoted to military adjutant of Chaozhou—was sent down again to registrar of Yazhou, and Li Hui, observation commissioner of Hunan, was demoted to prefect of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 前鳳翔節度使石雄詣政府自陳黑山、烏嶺之功，求一鎮以終老。

translations.literal: Shi Xiong, former military governor of Fengxiang, came to the government to state in person his achievements at Heishan and Wuling, and asked for one commandery in which to end his days.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xiong, former military governor of Fengxiang, came before the court to recount his victories at Heishan and Wuling and asked for one frontier post where he might live out his days.

sentences.zh: 執政以雄李德裕所薦，曰：「向日之功，朝廷蒲、孟、岐三鎮酬之，足矣。」

translations.literal: Those in power, because Xiong had been recommended by Li Deyu, said: "For past achievements, the court has already rewarded him with the three commands of Pu, Meng, and Qi—that is enough."
translations.idiomatic: The ministers, noting that Xiong had been Li Deyu's protégé, said: "The court already rewarded his past service with the three commands of Pu, Meng, and Qi—that is enough."

sentences.zh: 除左神武統軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Commander of the Left Divine Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Commander of the Left Divine Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 雄怏怏而薨。

translations.literal: Xiong, resentful, died.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong died, bitter and disheartened.

sentences.zh: 十一月，庚午，萬壽公主適起居郎鄭顥。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day gengwu, Princess Wanshou was given in marriage to Zheng Hao, Attendant of the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on gengwu, Princess Wanshou was given in marriage to Zheng Hao, Attendant of the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 顥，絪之孫，登進士第，為校書郎、右拾遺內供奉，以文雅著稱。

translations.literal: Hao was the grandson of Yin. He passed the jinshi examination, served as collator and Right Remonstrance Officer on inner palace duty, and was renowned for literary refinement.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was a grandson of Zheng Yin. He had passed the jinshi examination, served as collator and Right Remonstrance Officer on inner palace duty, and was known for literary grace.

sentences.zh: 公主，上之愛女，故選顥尚之。

translations.literal: The princess was the emperor's beloved daughter, and so Hao was chosen to marry her.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was the emperor's favorite daughter, and so Hao was chosen as her husband.

sentences.zh: 有司循舊制請用銀裝車，上曰：「吾欲以儉約化天下，當自親者始。」

translations.literal: The responsible offices, following old regulations, requested the use of a silver-decorated carriage. The emperor said: "I wish to transform the realm through thrift—this must begin with those nearest to me."
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices, following precedent, requested a silver-decorated bridal carriage. The emperor said: "I mean to teach thrift to the realm, and that must begin with my own kin."

sentences.zh: 令依外命婦以銅裝車。

translations.literal: He ordered that, as with wives of outer nobility, a copper-decorated carriage be used.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a copper-decorated carriage, as used by wives of outer nobility.

sentences.zh: 詔公主執婦禮，皆如臣庶之法，戒以毋得輕夫族，毋得預時事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the princess to observe wifely rites entirely according to the laws for subjects and commoners, admonishing her not to slight her husband's clan and not to meddle in current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commanded the princess to observe wifely rites exactly as common subjects did, warning her not to slight her husband's family and not to meddle in affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 又申以手詔曰：「苟違吾戒，必有太平、安樂之禍。」

translations.literal: He further reiterated by personal edict: "If you violate my admonitions, you will surely meet the calamity of Taiping and Anle."
translations.idiomatic: He reinforced the command in a personal edict: "If you defy my warning, you will bring down the fate of Princess Taiping and Princess Anle upon yourself."

sentences.zh: 顥弟顗，嘗得危疾，上遣使視之。

translations.literal: Hao's younger brother Yi once fell gravely ill, and the emperor sent an envoy to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao's younger brother Yi fell gravely ill, the emperor sent an envoy to inquire after him.

sentences.zh: 還，問「公主何在？」

translations.literal: On returning, he asked: "Where is the princess?"
translations.idiomatic: On his return, the emperor asked, "Where is the princess?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「在慈恩寺觀戲場。」

translations.literal: He was told: "She is at Cien Temple watching the play ground."
translations.idiomatic: He was told, "At Cien Temple, watching a performance."

sentences.zh: 上怒，歎曰：「我怪士大夫家不欲與我家為昏，良有以也！」

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and sighed, saying: "I wondered why the households of scholar-officials did not wish to marry into my house—now I see they had good reason!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and sighed: "No wonder gentry families did not want to marry into the imperial house—they had their reasons!"

sentences.zh: 亟命召公主入宮，立之階下，不之視。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered the princess summoned to the palace, had her stand below the steps, and would not look at her.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered the princess brought to the palace, had her stand below the steps, and refused to look at her.

sentences.zh: 公主懼，涕泣謝罪。

translations.literal: The princess was afraid; weeping, she begged forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was terrified. Weeping, she begged forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 上責之曰：「豈有小郎病，不往省視，乃觀戲乎！」

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked her, saying: "When your young brother-in-law is ill, you do not go to visit him, and instead go watch a play!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked her: "Your young brother-in-law is ill, and you do not go to see him—you go watch a play instead?"

sentences.zh: 遣婦鄭氏。

translations.literal: He sent her away as a wife of the Zheng clan.
translations.idiomatic: He sent her back to the Zheng household.

sentences.zh: 由是終上之世，貴戚皆兢兢守禮法，如山東衣冠之族。

translations.literal: From this, throughout the rest of the emperor's reign, the imperial in-laws all kept to ritual and law with fearful care, like the gentry families of the eastern provinces.
translations.idiomatic: From then until the end of his reign, the imperial in-laws all observed ritual and law with anxious care, like the gentry families of the eastern provinces.

sentences.zh: 壬午，葬懿安皇后於景陵之側。

translations.literal: On the day renwu, Empress Yian was buried beside Jing Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, Empress Yian was buried beside Jing Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 以中書侍郎、同平章事韋琮為太子賓客、分司。

translations.literal: Wei Cong, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Head of Government Affairs, was appointed Crown Prince's Mentor with duty at the secondary capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Cong, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Head of Government Affairs, was made Crown Prince's Mentor with duty at the secondary capital.

sentences.zh: 十二月，鳳翔節度使崔珙奏破吐蕃，克清水。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Cui Gong, military governor of Fengxiang, reported defeating the Tibetans and capturing Qingshui.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Cui Gong, military governor of Fengxiang, reported a victory over the Tibetans and the capture of Qingshui.

sentences.zh: 清水先隸秦州，詔以本州未復，權隸鳳翔。

translations.literal: Qingshui had formerly been subordinate to Qinzhou; an edict ordered that, because that prefecture had not yet been recovered, it should temporarily be subordinated to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Qingshui had formerly belonged to Qinzhou, but an edict ordered that, since that prefecture had not yet been recovered, it should temporarily be placed under Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 上見憲宗朝公卿子孫，多擢用之。

translations.literal: The emperor noticed many descendants of ministers from Xianzong's reign and promoted them extensively.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor noticed many descendants of Xianzong's ministers and promoted them widely.

sentences.zh: 刑部員外郎杜勝次對，上問其家世，對曰：「臣父黃裳，首請憲宗監國。」

translations.literal: Du Sheng, Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice, answered in secondary audience; the emperor asked his family background, and he replied: "My father Huang Shang was the first to request that Xianzong oversee the realm as regent."
translations.idiomatic: Du Sheng, Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice, answered in secondary audience. The emperor asked about his family, and he replied: "My father Huang Shang was the first to ask that Xianzong oversee the realm as regent."

sentences.zh: 即除給事中。

translations.literal: He was immediately appointed Gentleman Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately appointed Gentleman Attendant.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士裴諗，度之子也，上幸翰林，面除承旨。

translations.literal: Pei Shen, a Hanlin Academician and son of Pei Du—when the emperor visited the Hanlin Academy, he was appointed Chief Academician on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Shen, a Hanlin Academician and son of Pei Du, was appointed Chief Academician on the spot when the emperor visited the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃論恐熱遣其將恭羅急藏將兵二萬略地西鄙，尚婢婢遣其將拓跋懷光擊之於南谷，大破之，急藏降。

translations.literal: The Tibetan Lun Dore sent his general Gongluo Jizang to lead twenty thousand troops to raid the western frontier; Shang Bibi dispatched her general Tuoba Huaiguang to attack him at Southern Valley, routed him completely, and Jizang surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan Lun Dore sent his general Gongluo Jizang with twenty thousand troops to raid the western frontier. Shang Bibi dispatched her general Tuoba Huaiguang to meet him at Southern Valley, routed him completely, and Jizang surrendered.

sentences.zh: 宣宗至道昭肅孝皇帝下大中三年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong Zhi-dao Zhao Su the Filial, Part Two, Dazhong year 3 (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong, the Filial and Sagely, Dazhong year 3 (

sentences.zh: 己巳，公元八四九年）

translations.literal: jisi, CE 849)
translations.idiomatic: jisi, CE 849)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，上與宰相論元和循吏孰為第一，周墀曰：「臣嘗守土江西，聞觀察使韋丹功德被於八州，沒四十年，老稚歌思，如丹尚存。」

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, the emperor discussed with his chief ministers which of Yuanhe's conscientious local officials ranked first; Zhou Chi said: "When I served in Jiangxi, I heard that Observation Commissioner Wei Dan's virtue and merit extended through eight prefectures; though dead forty years, the old and young still sang of him with longing, as if Dan were still alive."
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, the emperor asked his chief ministers which of Yuanhe's conscientious local officials ranked first. Zhou Chi said: "When I served in Jiangxi, I heard that Observation Commissioner Wei Dan's virtue and merit had spread through eight prefectures. Though he had been dead forty years, the old and young still sang of him with longing, as if Dan were still alive."

sentences.zh: 乙亥，詔史館修撰杜牧撰《丹遺愛碑》以紀之，仍擢其子河陽觀察判官宙為御史。

translations.literal: On yihai, an edict ordered Du Mu, Compiler of the Historiography Institute, to compose the Stele of Dan's Enduring Kindness to record this; Wei Dan's son Zhou, administrative aide to the Heyang observation commission, was also promoted to Censor.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, an edict ordered Du Mu, Compiler of the Historiography Institute, to compose the Stele of Dan's Enduring Kindness in his honor. Wei Dan's son Zhou, administrative aide to the Heyang observation commission, was also promoted to Censor.

sentences.zh: 二月，吐蕃論恐熱軍於河州，尚婢婢軍於河源軍。

translations.literal: In the second month, the Tibetan Lun Dore encamped at Hezhou, and Shang Bibi encamped at Heyuan Fortress.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, the Tibetan Lun Dore encamped at Hezhou, and Shang Bibi encamped at Heyuan Fortress.

sentences.zh: 婢婢諸將欲擊恐熱，婢婢曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Bibi's generals wished to attack Lun Dore; Bibi said: "It cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Bibi's generals wanted to attack Lun Dore, but Bibi said: "No.

sentences.zh: 我軍驟勝而輕敵，彼窮困而致死，戰必不利。」

translations.literal: Our army, flush with sudden victory, will treat the enemy lightly; theirs, cornered and desperate, will fight to the death—the battle will surely go against us."
translations.idiomatic: Our army, flush with sudden victory, will treat the enemy lightly; theirs, cornered and desperate, will fight to the death. The battle will surely go against us."

sentences.zh: 諸將不從。

translations.literal: The generals did not obey.
translations.idiomatic: The generals would not listen.

sentences.zh: 婢婢知其必敗，據河橋以待之，諸將果敗。

translations.literal: Bibi, knowing they would certainly be defeated, held the river bridge waiting for them; the generals were indeed defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Bibi, knowing they would be defeated, held the river bridge and waited. The generals were routed, just as she had foreseen.

sentences.zh: 婢婢收餘眾，焚橋，歸鄯州。

translations.literal: Bibi gathered the remaining forces, burned the bridge, and returned to Zhaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bibi gathered the survivors, burned the bridge, and withdrew to Zhaozhou.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃秦、原、安樂三州及石門等七關來降。

translations.literal: The three Tibetan prefectures of Qin, Yuan, and Anle, together with the seven passes including Shimen, came over in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The three prefectures of Qin, Yuan, and Anle, together with the seven passes including Shimen, surrendered from Tibetan control.

sentences.zh: 以太僕卿陸耽為宜諭使，詔涇原、寧武、鳳翔、邠寧、振武皆出兵應接。

translations.literal: Lu Gan, Grand Master of Horse, was appointed Commissioner of Pacification and Proclamation; an edict ordered Jingyuan, Ningwu, Fengxiang, Binning, and Zhenwu all to dispatch troops in support.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Gan, Grand Master of Horse, was appointed Commissioner of Pacification and Proclamation. An edict ordered Jingyuan, Ningwu, Fengxiang, Binning, and Zhenwu all to dispatch troops in support.

sentences.zh: 河東節度使王宰入朝，以貨結貴幸，求以使相領宣武。

translations.literal: Wang Zai, military governor of Hedong, came to court; through gifts he cultivated the favored and powerful, and sought to take Xuanwu as a commissioner concurrently bearing the title of chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zai, military governor of Hedong, came to court. Through gifts he cultivated the emperor's favorites and sought to take command of Xuanwu as a commissioner-chancellor.

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書、同平章事周墀上疏論之，宰遂還鎮。

translations.literal: Zhou Chi, Minister of Justice and Co-Head of Government Affairs, submitted a memorial criticizing this, and Zai thereupon returned to his command.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chi, Minister of Justice and Co-Head of Government Affairs, submitted a memorial criticizing the request, and Zai returned to his command.

sentences.zh: 附馬都尉韋讓求為京兆尹，墀言京兆尹非才望不可為，讓議意寢。

translations.literal: Wei Rang, imperial son-in-law, sought appointment as Jingzhao Intendant; Chi said the Jingzhao Intendant could not be filled without talent and reputation, and Rang's proposal was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Rang, an imperial son-in-law, sought appointment as Jingzhao Intendant. Chi argued that the post required talent and reputation, and Rang's proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 墀又諫上開邊，由是忤旨。

translations.literal: Chi also remonstrated against the emperor's frontier campaigns, and for this ran afoul of the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Chi also remonstrated against the emperor's frontier campaigns, and for this ran afoul of the throne.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，以墀為東川節度使，以御史大夫崔鉉為中書侍郎、同平章事，兵部侍郎、判戶部魏扶同平章事。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Chi was appointed military governor of Dongchuan; Cui Xuan, Chief Censor, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Head of Government Affairs; Wei Fu, Vice Director of the Ministry of War and Acting Director of the Ministry of Revenue, was made Co-Head of Government Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Chi was appointed military governor of Dongchuan. Cui Xuan, Chief Censor, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Head of Government Affairs, and Wei Fu, Vice Director of the Ministry of War and Acting Director of the Ministry of Revenue, was made Co-Head of Government Affairs.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，盧龍奏節度使張仲武薨，軍中立其子節度押牙直方。

translations.literal: On guisi, Lulong reported that military governor Zhang Zhongwu had died; the army installed his son Zhifang, chief military adjutant of the command, as governor.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, Lulong reported that military governor Zhang Zhongwu had died. The army installed his son Zhifang, chief military adjutant of the command, as governor.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士鄭顥言於上曰：「周墀以直言入相，亦以直言罷相。」

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Zheng Hao said to the emperor: "Zhou Chi entered the chancellorship through upright speech, and left the chancellorship through upright speech as well."
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Zheng Hao said to the emperor: "Zhou Chi entered the chancellorship through upright speech, and left it through upright speech as well."

sentences.zh: 上深感悟，甲午，墀入謝，加檢校右僕射。

translations.literal: The emperor was deeply moved to reflection; on jiawu, Chi came to give thanks for his appointment and was given the additional title of acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply moved. On jiawu, Chi came to give thanks for his appointment and was given the additional title of acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，以張直方為盧龍留後。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Zhang Zhifang was made acting governor of Lulong.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Zhang Zhifang was made acting governor of Lulong.

sentences.zh: 五月，徐州軍亂，逐節度使李廓。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the armies of Xuzhou mutinied and drove out military governor Li Kuo.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, the armies of Xuzhou mutinied and drove out military governor Li Kuo.

sentences.zh: 廓，程之子也，在鎮不治。

translations.literal: Kuo was the son of Cheng and had not governed well in command.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo was Cheng's son and had governed poorly in command.

sentences.zh: 右補闕鄭魯上言其狀，且曰：「臣恐新麥未登，徐師必亂。

translations.literal: Zheng Lu, Right Supplementation Censor, set forth the situation in a memorial, adding: "I fear that if the new wheat is not yet harvested, the troops of Xu will surely revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Lu, Right Supplementation Censor, set forth the situation in a memorial, adding: "I fear that before the new wheat is harvested, the troops of Xu will surely revolt.

sentences.zh: 速命良帥，救此一方。」

translations.literal: Appoint a capable commander at once and save this region."
translations.idiomatic: Appoint a capable commander at once and save this region."

sentences.zh: 上未之省。

translations.literal: The emperor did not take his meaning to heart.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 徐州果亂，上思魯言，擢為起居舍人。

translations.literal: Xuzhou did indeed revolt; the emperor recalled Lu's words and promoted him to Attendant of Daily Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou did indeed revolt. The emperor recalled Lu's warning and promoted him to Attendant of Daily Affairs.

sentences.zh: 以義成節度使盧弘止為武寧節度使。

translations.literal: Lu Hongzhi, military governor of Yicheng, was appointed military governor of Wuning.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Hongzhi, military governor of Yicheng, was appointed military governor of Wuning.

sentences.zh: 武寧士卒素驕，有銀刀都尤甚，屢逐主帥。

translations.literal: The soldiers of Wuning had long been haughty; the Silver Blade unit above all, and they had repeatedly driven off commanders.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers of Wuning had long been unruly; the Silver Blade unit worst of all, and they had repeatedly driven off their commanders.

sentences.zh: 弘止至鎮，都虞候胡慶方復謀作亂，弘止誅之，撫循其餘，訓以忠義，軍府由是獲安。

translations.literal: When Hongzhi arrived at his command, Chief Commandant Hu Qingfang again plotted mutiny; Hongzhi executed him, soothed and comforted the rest, and instructed them in loyalty and righteousness—and so the army and headquarters were thereafter secure.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongzhi arrived, Chief Commandant Hu Qingfang plotted mutiny again. Hongzhi executed him, soothed the rest, and instructed them in loyalty and righteousness. The army and headquarters were thereafter secure.

sentences.zh: 六月，戊申，以張直方為盧龍節度使。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on wushen, Zhang Zhifang was appointed military governor of Lulong.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on wushen, Zhang Zhifang was appointed military governor of Lulong.

sentences.zh: 涇原節度使康季榮取原州及石門、驛藏、木峽、制勝、六磐、石峽六關。

translations.literal: Kang Jirong, military governor of Jingyuan, took Yuanzhou and the six passes of Shimen, Yizang, Muxia, Zhisheng, Liupan, and Shixia.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Jirong, military governor of Jingyuan, took Yuanzhou and the six passes of Shimen, Yizang, Muxia, Zhisheng, Liupan, and Shixia.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丁巳，靈武節度使朱叔明聚長樂州。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on dingsi, Zhu Shuming, military governor of Lingwu, consolidated Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on dingsi, Zhu Shuming, military governor of Lingwu, consolidated control of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 甲子，邠寧節度使張君緒取蕭關。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Zhang Junxu, military governor of Binning, took Xiao Pass.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, Zhang Junxu, military governor of Binning, took Xiao Pass.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，鳳翔節度使李玭取秦州。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Li Pin, military governor of Fengxiang, took Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Li Pin, military governor of Fengxiang, took Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔邠寧節度權移軍於寧州以應接河西。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Binning garrison temporarily to move its army to Ningzhou to support the Hexi front.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Binning garrison temporarily to move its army to Ningzhou to support the Hexi front.

sentences.zh: 八月，乙酉，改長樂州為威州。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on yiyou, Changzhou was renamed Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on yiyou, Changzhou was renamed Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 河、隴老幼千餘人詣闕，己丑，上御延喜門樓見之，歡呼舞躍，解胡服，襲冠帶，觀者皆呼萬歲。

translations.literal: More than a thousand old and young from He and Long came to the capital; on jichou the emperor mounted the tower of the Yanxi Gate to receive them; they shouted for joy and danced; doffing barbarian dress, they put on caps and sashes, and onlookers all cried ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand old and young from He and Long came to the capital. On jichou the emperor mounted the tower of the Yanxi Gate to receive them. They shouted for joy and danced, doffing barbarian dress and putting on caps and sashes, while onlookers all cried ten thousand years.

sentences.zh: 詔「募百姓墾闢三州、七關土田，五年不租稅，自今京城罪人應配流者皆配十處。

translations.literal: An edict ordered: "Recruit common people to reclaim and open the farmland of the three prefectures and seven passes; for five years no rent or tax shall be levied; from now on, criminals in the capital who ought to be sentenced to exile shall all be sent to these ten places.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered: "Recruit common people to reclaim the farmland of the three prefectures and seven passes. For five years no rent or tax shall be levied. From now on, criminals in the capital sentenced to exile shall all be sent to these ten places.

sentences.zh: 四道將吏能於鎮戍之地為營田者，官給牛及種糧，溫池鹽利可贍邊陲，委度支制置。

translations.literal: Military officers of the four circuits who can establish garrison farmlands in defended areas shall receive oxen and seed grain from the government; the salt profits of Warm Springs Pool can supply the frontier—this shall be arranged by the Directorate of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Military officers of the four circuits who can establish garrison farmlands in defended areas shall receive oxen and seed grain from the government. The salt profits of Warm Springs Pool can supply the frontier, and this shall be arranged by the Directorate of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 其三州、七關鎮戍之卒，皆倍給衣糧，仍二年一代。

translations.literal: The garrison soldiers defending the three prefectures and seven passes shall all receive double clothing and provisions, and tours of duty shall rotate every two years.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison soldiers defending the three prefectures and seven passes shall all receive double clothing and provisions, with tours of duty rotating every two years.

sentences.zh: 道路建置堡柵，有商旅往來販易及戍卒子弟通傳家信，關鎮毋得留難。

translations.literal: Forts and stockades shall be established along the roads; merchants traveling to trade and the sons and younger brothers of garrison soldiers passing family letters—pass and barrier officials may not obstruct them.
translations.idiomatic: Forts and stockades shall be established along the roads. Merchants traveling to trade and the sons and younger brothers of garrison soldiers carrying family letters may not be obstructed by pass and barrier officials.

sentences.zh: 其山南、劍南邊境有沒蕃州縣，亦令量力收復。」

translations.literal: Where prefectures and counties on the southern Shannan and Jiannan frontier have fallen to Tibet, they are likewise ordered to recover what they can according to local strength."
translations.idiomatic: Where prefectures and counties on the southern Shannan and Jiannan frontier have fallen to Tibet, they are likewise ordered to recover what they can according to local strength."

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，改備邊庫為延資庫。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, the Border Defense Reserve Treasury was renamed the Extended Resources Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, the Border Defense Reserve Treasury was renamed the Extended Resources Treasury.

sentences.zh: 西川節充使杜悰奏取維州。

translations.literal: Du Cong, military governor of Xichuan, reported recovering Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Du Cong, military governor of Xichuan, reported recovering Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 閏十一月，丁酉，宰相以克復河、湟，請上尊號。

translations.literal: In the intercalary eleventh month, on dingyou, the chief ministers, because the He and Huang regions had been recovered, requested that the emperor accept an honorific title.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary eleventh month, on dingyou, the chief ministers, because the He and Huang regions had been recovered, requested that the emperor accept an honorific title.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「憲宗常有志復河、湟，以中原方用兵，未遂而崩，今乃克成先志耳。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Xianzong long cherished the aim of recovering He and Huang, but the Central Plains were then at war and he died before achieving it; now we have simply fulfilled his former intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Xianzong long cherished the aim of recovering He and Huang, but the Central Plains were then at war and he died before achieving it. We have now simply fulfilled his former intent.

sentences.zh: 其議加順、憲二廟尊謚以昭功烈。」

translations.literal: Let the discussion instead add posthumous honorific titles for the temples of Shun and Xian to manifest their achievements."
translations.idiomatic: Let the discussion instead add posthumous honorific titles for the temples of Shun and Xian to manifest their achievements."

sentences.zh: 盧龍節度使張直方，暴忍，喜遊獵。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhifang, military governor of Lulong, was violent and cruel and fond of hunting.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhifang, military governor of Lulong, was violent and cruel and fond of hunting.

sentences.zh: 軍中將作亂，直方知之，託言出獵，遂舉族逃歸京師。

translations.literal: When the army was about to mutiny, Zhifang learned of it; claiming he was going out to hunt, he fled with his entire clan back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the army was about to mutiny, Zhifang learned of it. Claiming he was going out to hunt, he fled with his entire clan back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 軍中推牙將周綝為留後，直方至京師，拜金吾大將軍。

translations.literal: The army installed the junior officer Zhou Lin as acting governor; Zhifang reached the capital and was appointed Grand General of the Gold Wu Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The army installed the junior officer Zhou Lin as acting governor. Zhifang reached the capital and was appointed Grand General of the Gold Wu Guard.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，追上順宗謚曰至德弘道大聖大安孝皇帝，憲宗謚曰昭文章武大聖至神孝皇帝。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, the posthumous title of Emperor Shunzong was established as Emperor Zhide Hongdao Dasheng Da'an the Filial, and that of Emperor Xianzong as Emperor Zhao Wen Zhangwu Dasheng Zhishen the Filial.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Emperor Shunzong was given the posthumous title Emperor Zhide Hongdao Dasheng Da'an the Filial, and Emperor Xianzong the posthumous title Emperor Zhao Wen Zhangwu Dasheng Zhishen the Filial.

sentences.zh: 仍改題神主。

translations.literal: The spirit tablets were likewise reinscribed.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit tablets were likewise reinscribed.

sentences.zh: 己未，崖州司戶李德裕卒。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Li Deyu, Registrar of Yazhou, died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, Li Deyu, Registrar of Yazhou, died.

sentences.zh: 山南西道節度使鄭涯奏取扶州。

translations.literal: Zheng Ya, military governor of Shannan West Circuit, reported recovering Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Ya, military governor of Shannan West Circuit, reported recovering Fuzhou.
